definition_zh: 艺术家；画家；表演者；能手
definition_en: a person who creates art, performs, or does something with great skill
core_image: 衣袖沾着颜料，手里握着画笔
scene: 画室的窗开着，颜料味很重。The artist worked standing up for six hours.
sceneCN: 这里 artist 是「画家」（第 1 个义项：从事绘画等造型艺术的人）；句意是这位画家站着画了六个小时。

pos.zh: 名词：艺术家；表演者；能手

senses.title: A maker of visual art
senses.definition: someone who paints, draws, or makes sculpture
senses.definitionCN: 从事绘画或雕塑创作的人
senses.example: The artist worked standing up for six hours.
senses.exampleCN: 这位画家站着画了六个小时。
senses.why: French artiste came from Latin ars, 'skill'; the word first named anyone skilled, then those skilled in art.
senses.whyCN: 法语 artiste 源自拉丁语 ars「技艺」；这个词先指任何有技艺的人，后专指艺术上有技艺的人。

senses.title: A performer
senses.definition: a singer, dancer, or actor who performs for an audience
senses.definitionCN: 为观众表演的歌手、舞者或演员
senses.example: The artist came back for a second song.
senses.exampleCN: 这位歌手返场又唱了一首。
senses.why: Music and stage work are also arts, so the performer is an artist in the same old sense of trained skill.
senses.whyCN: 音乐与舞台同样是艺术，所以表演者仍是「有训练技艺之人」这一古老意义上的艺术家。

senses.title: Someone very skilled
senses.definition: a person who does something with unusual skill
senses.definitionCN: 把某事做得格外有本领的人
senses.example: He is an artist at finding cheap flights.
senses.exampleCN: 他找便宜机票是个高手。
senses.why: Since art once meant any craft, calling someone an artist praises the skill rather than the medium.
senses.whyCN: 既然 art 本指任何手艺，称某人为 artist 就是在夸技艺，而非指门类。

intro.en: Artist came to English through French and Italian from the Latin word for skill.
intro.cn: artist 经法语与意大利语进入英语，源头是拉丁语的「技艺」一词。

items.en: ars meant 'skill, craft'.
items.cn: ars 意为「技艺、手艺」。

items.en: artista named a skilled maker or scholar.
items.cn: artista 指有技艺的制作者或学者。

items.en: artiste carried the word into French.
items.cn: artiste 把词带入法语。

items.en: English artist first meant a master of any craft.
items.cn: 英语 artist 最初指任何手艺的行家。

items.en: The word narrowed to painters and then widened to performers.
items.cn: 这个词先缩小到画家，后又扩展到表演者。

note.en: The look-alike group is the art family; the near-meaning group names other makers and performers.
note.cn: 形近组是 art 词族；近义组是其他创作者与表演者。

sensesIntro.en: Skill in making, skill on stage, and skill anywhere share one word.

intro.en: A French and Italian word built on the Latin root for skill.

definition_zh: 艺术的；有艺术才华的；有审美品味的
definition_en: relating to art, or showing natural skill and taste in art
core_image: 眼睛先在心里构图，再动手
scene: 房间的摆设并不贵，却处处有讲究。The whole room has an artistic feel.
sceneCN: 这里 artistic 是「有艺术气息的」（第 2 个义项：显出艺术才华与品味）；句意是整个房间有一种艺术气息。

pos.zh: 形容词：艺术的；有艺术才华的

senses.title: Relating to art
senses.definition: connected with art or with artists
senses.definitionCN: 与艺术或艺术家相关的
senses.example: The city has a strong artistic tradition.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市有深厚的艺术传统。
senses.why: Artist plus -ic makes an adjective of belonging: whatever belongs to artists or their work is artistic.
senses.whyCN: artist 加 -ic 构成表示归属的形容词：属于艺术家或其作品的东西就是「艺术的」。

senses.title: Showing artistic gift
senses.definition: naturally good at making or judging beautiful things
senses.definitionCN: 天生擅长创作或鉴赏美的事物
senses.example: The whole room has an artistic feel.
senses.exampleCN: 整个房间有一种艺术气息。
senses.why: The same adjective shifts from belonging to possessing: a person or place can show the quality itself.
senses.whyCN: 同一个形容词从「属于」转向「具有」：人或场所本身可以显出这种品质。

intro.en: Artistic is a modern adjective formed on artist.
intro.cn: artistic 是在 artist 之上构成的近代形容词。

items.en: ars meant 'skill, craft'.
items.cn: ars 意为「技艺、手艺」。

items.en: artista named a skilled maker.

items.en: English artist settled in the sixteenth century.

items.en: The adjective artistic appeared with the rise of art criticism.
items.cn: 随着艺术批评兴起，形容词 artistic 出现。

items.en: It now describes both art itself and people with taste.
items.cn: 如今它既修饰艺术本身，也形容有品味的人。

note.en: The look-alike group is the artist family; the near-meaning group gives words of taste and beauty.
note.cn: 形近组是 artist 词族；近义组是表示品味与美的词。

normal.en: Artistic merit judges a work's value.
normal.cn: artistic merit 用来评判作品的价值。

normal.en: The adverb adds -ally, not -ly.

abstract.en: See paint marks left deliberately rough.

dict_mnemonic.text: artist（艺术家）加 -ic：与艺术家或艺术相关的，就是艺术的。

root: 由 artist 加形容词后缀 -ic 构成；artist 经法语与意大利语源自拉丁语 ars「技艺」。

sensesIntro.en: Belonging to art and possessing art are two sides of one adjective.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an eye composing a picture before the hand begins.

intro.en: A nineteenth-century adjective grown from the noun artist.

latinIntro.en: The root ars, 'skill', underlies the whole family.

definition_zh: 艺术技巧；艺术性；精湛技艺
definition_en: great skill and creativity in an art or craft
core_image: 指尖在琴键上流出的灵光
scene: 老工匠打磨着琴身，木纹在灯下泛着琥珀光。Visitors admired the artistry of the carved doorway.
sceneCN: 这里 artistry 是「精湛技艺」（第 1 个义项：艺术性的高超技巧）；句意是来访者赞叹雕花门廊的精美工艺。

pos.zh: 艺术性；巧夺天工的品质

derivatives.zh: 基础词，义为「艺术家」，artistry 由其加后缀 -ry 构成

senses.title: Great artistic skill
senses.definition: exceptional ability and creative skill in performing or making
senses.definitionCN: 表演或创作中超凡的能力与创造性技巧
senses.example: The pianist played with effortless artistry.
senses.exampleCN: 钢琴家的演奏挥洒自如、技艺精湛。
senses.why: The suffix -ry names the quality or practice of the artist.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ry 表示「艺术家之特质或实践」。

senses.title: Artistic quality in a work
senses.definition: the degree to which a work shows beauty, imagination and craft
senses.definitionCN: 作品体现美感、想象与匠心的程度
senses.example: The film's artistry lies in its silent long shots.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片的艺术性在于其无声的长镜头。
senses.why: The quality of the maker transfers to the made object.
senses.whyCN: 制作者的气质转移到作品之上。

intro.en: Artistry is artist plus the noun suffix -ry, formed within English in the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: artistry 由 artist 加名词后缀 -ry 构成，19 世纪在英语内部生成。

items.en: Root *h2er- (to fit together) is reconstructed behind Latin ars.
items.cn: 重构词根 *h2er-（接合）位于拉丁语 ars 之下（重构形式）。

items.en: Ars meant skill, craft, method, the trained way of doing anything well.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ars 意为技艺、方法，指把任何事做好的训练之道。

items.en: Old French art broadened the word toward fine art and learned skill.
items.cn: 古法语 art 使词义向美术与学问之技扩展。

items.en: Artistry formed on the model of artistry-like nouns in -ry, first recorded about 1837.
items.cn: artistry 仿 -ry 系名词构成，约 1837 年首见记载。

items.en: It now praises creative skill wherever it appears, from kitchens to code.
items.cn: 如今它赞美一切创造性技艺，从厨房到代码。

note.en: Artistry names the quality; artist the person; artistic the style.
note.cn: artistry 指品质，artist 指人，artistic 指风格。

entries.definition: a skilled manual craftsman
entries.definitionCN: 工匠，与 artistry 同出拉丁 ars 但指手艺人

entries.definition: a person who creates art

entries.definitionCN: 手艺、工艺，与 artistry 义近而更重手上功夫

entries.definition: delicate skill and subtlety in handling
entries.definitionCN: 细腻精妙的技巧，与 artistry 义近

entries.definition: complete command of a skill
entries.definitionCN: 精通、驾驭自如，与 artistry 义近而泛指技艺

normalIntro.en: Build the word visibly: artist + ry = the artist's quality.
normalIntro.cn: 直观构词：artist + ry ＝ 艺术家之特质。

normal.en: artist + -ry = artistry, the quality of being artistic.
normal.cn: artist + -ry ＝ artistry，即艺术造诣。

normal.en: -ry builds quality nouns: bravery, robbery, artistry.
normal.cn: -ry 构成性质名词：bravery、robbery、artistry。

normal.en: Sheer artistry praises effortless perfection.
normal.cn: sheer artistry 赞叹浑然天成的完美。

normal.en: Compare artisan (craftsman) with artist (creator).
normal.cn: 对比 artisan（工匠）与 artist（创作者）。

normal.en: Adjective is artistic, not artistry-like.
normal.cn: 形容词是 artistic。

abstract.en: Watch a brush lift at exactly the right moment.
abstract.cn: 看画笔在最恰当的一瞬提起。

abstract.en: Hear a voice bend a single note into something new.
abstract.cn: 听一个音符在嗓音中被折出新的形状。

abstract.en: See wood shavings curling from a carver's blade like ribbons.
abstract.cn: 想象雕刀下木屑如缎带般卷起。

examples.en: The pastry chef's artistry drew crowds at the expo.
examples.cn: 糕点师的精湛手艺在博览会上吸引了大批观众。

examples.en: Critics praised the novel's narrative artistry.
examples.cn: 评论家盛赞这部小说的叙事艺术。

examples.en: There is real artistry in the way he codes.
examples.cn: 他写代码的方式颇具匠心。

root: 拉丁语 ars（技艺）→ 古法语 art → 英语 artist → artist + -ry（性质名词后缀）→ artistry；-ry 同族词有 bravery、jewelry。

sensesIntro.en: From the artist's exceptional skill to the artistic quality of a work.
sensesIntro.cn: 由艺术家的超凡技艺延伸到作品呈现的艺术性。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: inspiration flowing from trained fingertips
core.cn: 核心意象：从训练有素的指尖流出的灵光

branches.en: artistry as measure of a work
branches.cn: 作为作品尺度的艺术性

intro.en: The suffix -ry turns nouns of person into nouns of quality or place.
intro.cn: 后缀 -ry 把指人名词变成性质或场所名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin ars traveled through French art into the whole art family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ars 经法语 art 延伸出整个 art 词族。

definition_zh: n. 工艺品；美术器皿（统称，不可数）
definition_en: Decorative objects such as ceramics, glass and metal pieces considered together as a class of goods rather than as single works.
core_image: 货架上一排排只为好看而做的瓶瓶罐罐
scene: 橱窗里摆着一排青瓷花瓶与铜盘。The window displayed Chinese artware in blue and bronze.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：artware 是工艺品的统称，把它当一类货品来看，而不是单件作品。

senses.title: Decorative objects as a class
senses.titleCN: 作为一类货品的装饰器物
senses.definition: ceramics, glass, metal and similar pieces made mainly to be looked at, spoken of together
senses.definitionCN: 主要为观赏而做的陶瓷、玻璃、金属等器物，作为一个整体来谈
senses.example: The museum shop sells local artware.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆商店出售本地工艺品。
senses.why: The second half, ware, means goods, so the word counts things by shelf rather than by masterpiece.
senses.whyCN: 后半 ware 意为「货品」，所以这个词是按货架而不是按杰作来数东西的。

senses.title: A trade category
senses.definition: the heading used in shops, catalogues and customs lists for decorative goods
senses.definitionCN: 商店、目录与报关清单上用来归类装饰性货品的名目
senses.example: Artware forms a separate line in the export list.
senses.exampleCN: 工艺品在出口清单上单列一项。
senses.why: Because the word names a class of goods, it fits invoices and catalogues where artwork would sound too grand.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词指的是一类货品，它适合发票与目录，而 artwork 在那里显得过于隆重。

intro.en: Artware joins art, from Latin ars, skill, to ware, from Old English waru, goods: skill turned into things for sale.
intro.cn: artware 由 art（源自拉丁语 ars「技艺」）与 ware（源自古英语 waru「货品」）拼成：技艺变成了可售的物件。

items.en: Latin ars meant skill or craft, the trained ability to make something well.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ars 意为「技艺、手艺」，即把东西做好的训练出来的能力。

items.en: Old French art carried the Latin sense of skill into the western languages.
items.cn: 古法语 art 把拉丁语「技艺」的意思带入西部各语言。

items.en: Old English waru meant goods or wares, the things a trader carries, and survives in hardware and silverware.
items.cn: 古英语 waru 意为「货品」，即商人携带之物，如今仍留在 hardware 与 silverware 中。

items.en: English ware came to name a whole class of made things, usually joined to the material or purpose.
items.cn: 英语 ware 转而指一整类制成品，通常与材料或用途拼合使用。

items.en: Nineteenth-century trade English joined the two halves to name decorative goods sold in quantity.
items.cn: 十九世纪的商贸英语把两半拼起来，指成批出售的装饰性货品。

items.en: Twentieth-century catalogues and customs lists kept artware as a heading beside ceramics and glassware.
items.cn: 二十世纪的目录与报关清单把 artware 与陶瓷、玻璃器皿并列，作为一个品类名目保留下来。

note.en: The look-alike group splits the two halves of the compound; the near-meaning group names the crafts that fill the shelf.
note.cn: 形近组把这个复合词的两半拆开来比；近义组列出填满货架的各类手艺名称。

entries.definitionCN: 一件完成的美术作品或插图。

entries.definition: Tools and metal goods, or computer parts.

normalIntro.en: Artware is art plus ware, goods: skill on a shelf, priced by the piece rather than hung in a gallery.
normalIntro.cn: artware 就是 art 加 ware「货品」：摆在货架上的技艺，按件标价，而不是挂进美术馆。

normal.en: Ware always means a class of goods.
normal.cn: ware 一律表示一类货品。

normal.en: Hardware, silverware and glassware follow the same pattern.
normal.cn: hardware、silverware、glassware 都是同一构词法。

normal.en: Artware is uncountable, so use a piece of artware.
normal.cn: artware 不可数，要说 a piece of artware。

normal.en: Artwork is one piece, artware is the whole shelf.
normal.cn: artwork 是一件，artware 是整架。

normal.en: The word belongs to shops and catalogues.
normal.cn: 这个词属于商店与商品目录。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf of blue vases waiting for buyers.
abstract.cn: 想象一架青花瓶等着买主。

abstract.en: Imagine a customs form with one box for decorative goods.
abstract.cn: 想象报关单上有一个「装饰货品」的格子。

abstract.en: Think of skill packed into a crate for shipping.
abstract.cn: 想象技艺被装箱待运。

examples.en: The stall was piled with painted artware.
examples.cn: 摊子上堆满彩绘工艺品。

examples.en: She buys artware whenever she travels.
examples.cn: 她每次旅行都会买工艺品。

examples.en: Artware and textiles fill the lower floor.
examples.cn: 工艺品与织物占满了下一层。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：art「艺术」+ ware「器皿、货品」——摆成货卖的艺术品，就是工艺品 artware。

root: 拉丁语 ars「技艺」经古法语 art 入英语；古英语 waru「货品」给出 ware；十九世纪商贸英语把两者拼成 artware，指成批出售的装饰器物。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses treat beauty as stock: objects made to be looked at, and the catalogue heading under which they are shipped and sold.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都把「美」当作库存：为观赏而做的器物，以及它们被运输与销售时所归入的目录名目。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: shelves of jars and vases made only to be looked at
core.cn: 核心意象：货架上一排排只为好看而做的瓶瓶罐罐

branches.en: Blue vases and bronze plates in a window.
branches.cn: 橱窗里的青花瓶与铜盘。

branches.en: A stall piled with painted pieces.
One line on an export list.
branches.cn: 出口清单上单列的一项。

branches.en: A heading beside ceramics and glassware.
branches.cn: 与陶瓷、玻璃器皿并列的名目。

branches.en: Beauty counted as stock, not as masterpieces.
branches.cn: 把美当库存来数，而不是当杰作。

intro.en: Artware is art plus -ware; the same goods ending builds hardware, glassware and silverware, while art adds -istic and -isan.
intro.cn: artware 是 art 加 -ware；同一「货品」后缀构成 hardware、glassware 与 silverware，而 art 一侧则派生出 -istic 与 -isan 一类形式。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is ars, skill, artifex, a skilled maker, and artificium, a crafted thing; the ware half stays Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 ars「技艺」、artifex「巧匠」与 artificium「手工制品」；ware 那一半仍是日耳曼来源。

latinEntries.example: Ars opens the whole art family.
latinEntries.exampleCN: ars 是整个 art 词族的起点。

definition_zh: v. 攀登；上升；登上（王位等）；（道路）向上倾斜
definition_en: To go up or climb towards a higher point; to rise to a higher rank or position; of a path, to slope upwards.
core_image: 脚一级一级往上踩，位置越来越高
scene: 缆车沿着陡坡缓缓爬升。The cable car began to ascend the steep slope.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：ascend 指往高处移动、攀登，比 climb 更正式。

senses.title: To go up towards a higher point
senses.definition: to climb or move upwards, a more formal word than climb
senses.definitionCN: 向上攀登或移动，比 climb 更正式
senses.example: We ascended the ridge before sunrise.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在日出前登上了山脊。
senses.why: The root means to climb, and the prefix means to, so the word paints movement directed at a height.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为「爬」，前缀意为「向」，所以这个词画的是朝着某个高处的移动。

senses.title: To rise to a higher position
senses.definition: to reach a higher rank, office or throne, without any physical climbing
senses.definitionCN: 取得更高的等级、职位或王位，不涉及身体的攀爬
senses.example: She ascended the throne at the age of twenty.
senses.exampleCN: 她二十岁登上王位。
senses.why: Height is the oldest metaphor for rank, so the climbing verb was borrowed for thrones and offices.
senses.whyCN: 「高」是最古老的地位隐喻，于是这个表示攀爬的动词被借去说王位与职位。

senses.title: To slope upwards
senses.definition: of a road, path or ground, to rise as it goes forward
senses.definitionCN: 指道路、小径或地面向前延伸时逐渐升高
senses.example: The track ascends sharply after the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 过了桥之后小路陡然上行。
senses.why: Here nothing moves at all: the shape of the ground itself is described as if it were climbing.
senses.whyCN: 这里其实什么都没动：地面的形状本身被描述成好像在往上爬。

intro.en: Ascend is Latin ascendere, from ad, to, plus scandere, to climb; the same climbing root gives descend, scale and scandal.
intro.cn: ascend 就是拉丁语 ascendere，由 ad「向」加 scandere「爬」构成；同一「爬」词根还给出 descend、scale 与 scandal。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning to jump or climb lies behind several words for going up and for stumbling.
items.cn: 一个拟构的印欧词根意为「跳、爬」，藏在若干表示上升与绊倒的词背后。

items.en: Latin scandere meant to climb, and also to scan verse by counting its steps.
items.cn: 拉丁语 scandere 意为「攀登」，也指按音步「划分诗句」。

items.en: With ad, to, the verb ascendere meant to climb up towards something.
items.cn: 加上 ad「向」之后，动词 ascendere 意为「朝某处往上爬」。

items.en: Old French kept the verb and passed it on with the sense of rising in rank as well as in space.
items.cn: 古法语保留了这个动词，并同时传递「地位上升」与「空间上升」两层意思。

items.en: English records ascend from the fourteenth century, at first mainly of climbing and of heavenly rising.
items.cn: 英语从十四世纪起记录 ascend，起初主要用于攀登与升天。

items.en: By the fifteenth century the verb was standard for reaching a throne or an office.
items.cn: 到十五世纪，这个动词已成为「登上王位或职位」的标准说法。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the climbing root and adds two words that only share the opening sound; the near-meaning group grades ways of going up.
note.cn: 形近组保留「爬」词根，并加上两个只是开头音相同的词；近义组按方式区分各种「往上」。

entries.definition: To go down from a higher place.
The act of going up, or an upward slope.
entries.definitionCN: 上升的动作，或向上的坡。

entries.definition: Severely self-disciplined, avoiding comfort.
To find out something for certain.
To go up using hands, feet or effort.
To move to a higher level or amount.
entries.definitionCN: 升到更高的位置或数量。

entries.definition: To go up, or to get onto something.
To climb something high and difficult.

normalIntro.en: Ascend is ad, to, plus scandere, climb: climbing towards something, whether a ridge or a throne.
normalIntro.cn: ascend 就是 ad「向」加 scandere「爬」：朝着某处往上爬，那处可以是山脊，也可以是王位。

normal.en: Descend is the same root turned downwards.
normal.cn: descend 是同一词根朝下的方向。

normal.en: Ascent is the noun, ascension the formal noun.
normal.cn: ascent 是名词，ascension 是更正式的名词。

normal.en: Ascend the throne needs no preposition.
normal.cn: ascend the throne 不需要介词。

normal.en: Ascend to power does need to.
normal.cn: ascend to power 则需要 to。

normal.en: Ascending order means from small to large.
normal.cn: ascending order 意为从小到大。

abstract.en: Picture feet finding one step after another.
abstract.cn: 想象双脚一级一级找到台阶。

abstract.en: Imagine a crown settling on a young head.
abstract.cn: 想象一顶王冠落在年轻的头上。

abstract.en: Think of a path that keeps tilting upward.
abstract.cn: 想象一条不断向上翘起的小路。

examples.en: The balloon ascended above the clouds.
examples.cn: 气球升到云层之上。

examples.en: He ascended to the directorship last spring.
examples.cn: 他去年春天升任主管。

examples.en: Sort the numbers in ascending order.
examples.cn: 把数字按升序排列。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：a-「向」+ scend「爬」——朝着高处爬，就是 ascend；换成 de-「向下」便成 descend。

root: 拉丁语 scandere「爬」加 ad-「向」构成 ascendere「向上攀」，经古法语入十四世纪英语；同根还有 descend「下降」、ascent「上升」与 scan「按音步划分」。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses are one upward line: a body climbing, a name rising in rank, and ground that tilts as it runs forward.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项是同一条向上的线：身体在攀、名位在升、地面向前延伸时向上翘。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: feet finding one step after another, ever higher
core.cn: 核心意象：脚一级一级往上踩，位置越来越高

branches.en: A crown settling on a young head.
A track tilting up after the bridge.
One upward line in space, rank and shape.
branches.cn: 空间、地位与形状中的同一条上行线。

intro.en: Ascend is a- from ad- plus -scend, climb; the same root builds descend, transcend, ascent and scan.
intro.cn: ascend 由 ad- 变来的 a- 加 -scend「爬」构成；同一词根还构成 descend、transcend、ascent 与 scan。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is scandere, to climb, ascendere, to climb up, and ascensus, a climbing; scala, a ladder, gives scale beside it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 scandere「爬」、ascendere「向上攀」与 ascensus「攀登」；旁边的 scala「梯子」产生 scale。

definition_zh: 查明；弄清；探明；核实；确定；确信；（古）告知；确保
definition_en: to find out something with certainty, to establish a fact or figure by investigation or measurement, and formerly to assure or inform someone
core_image: 桌上摊着一张写满传言的纸，有人提灯逐条划掉，直到只剩一行能被证实的字——那行字就是被“弄确定”的东西
scene: 检查员提着灯翻值班簿，要在一张划满线的纸上确认起火前谁还在楼里。The inspector says: We must ascertain who was in the building before the fire began.
sceneCN: 这里 ascertain 是「查明」（第 1 个义项：通过询问、核对或调查发现事实）；句意：我们必须查明起火之前谁在楼里。画面里有提灯、值班簿和一张划满线的纸。

pos.zh: 查明；弄清；探明；核实；确定

senses.title: Find out a fact
senses.titleCN: 查明：把传言问到只剩事实
senses.definition: to discover a fact or the truth by asking, checking or investigating
senses.definitionCN: 通过询问、核对或调查发现事实或真相
senses.example: The police are trying to ascertain how the door was opened.
senses.exampleCN: 警方正试图查明门是怎么被打开的。
senses.why: The modern sense 'find out for sure by experiment or investigation' is recorded by 1794, but the word began in the 15c. as 'to make certain'. Investigation is the method by which a matter is brought into certainty.
senses.whyCN: 现代义“通过实验或调查确实查明”记录于 1794 年，但这个词在 15 世纪原义是“使确定”。调查就是把一件事带到“确定”状态的方法。

senses.title: Fix a figure by measuring
senses.titleCN: 探明、测知：把不确定的量量成一个数
senses.definition: to establish a quantity, position or property by measurement or test
senses.definitionCN: 通过测量或检验确定数量、位置或性质
senses.example: Engineers ascertained the load the bridge could bear.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师探明了这座桥能承受的荷载。
senses.why: Latin certus means 'fixed, settled'. Measuring is literally fixing: before the test the load is unknown, after it the figure is settled and can be quoted.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 certus 义为“固定的、已定的”。测量就是字面上的“固定”：测试前荷载未知，测试后这个数被定下来，可以直接引用。

senses.title: Check a claim
senses.titleCN: 核实：把一句话拿去对证
senses.definition: to verify that a statement or report is true
senses.definitionCN: 核实某陈述或报告是否属实
senses.example: The editor could not ascertain whether the letter was genuine.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑无法核实这封信是否真实。
senses.why: The prefix a- (ad-, 'to') plus certain means 'bring to a sure state'. A claim is checked by being brought up against evidence until doubt is removed.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 a-（ad-，“向”）加 certain 义为“带到确定状态”。一句话被拿去与证据对照，直到疑点被去掉，才算核实。

senses.title: Reach a settled judgement
senses.titleCN: 断定：筛到最后，只剩一个结论
senses.definition: to determine something and come to be sure of it
senses.definitionCN: 确定某事并最终对其确信
senses.example: From the records we ascertained that the meeting had never taken place.
senses.exampleCN: 从记录看，我们断定那场会议从未举行。
senses.why: Latin certus came from cernere, 'to sift, separate, decide'. Ascertaining is a sifting: alternatives are removed until one remains, and the judgement inherits the sieve.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 certus 出自 cernere“筛、分开、判定”。ascertain 就是一次筛选：把其他可能一一去掉，直到只剩一个；判断继承了这把筛子。

senses.title: Pin down a person or thing
senses.titleCN: 查明（身份、下落）：把人或物定位到一个确定点
senses.definition: to find out who or where someone or something is
senses.definitionCN: 查明某人是谁或某物在哪里
senses.example: They ascertained the identity of the woman from a single photograph.
senses.exampleCN: 他们凭一张照片查明了那名女子的身份。
senses.why: The same act applied to a target: an unknown person is located and named. The 'fixed' quality of certus is what a name supplies — the person stops being an anonymous possibility.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动作用在目标上：一个未知的人被定位、被命名。certus 的“固定”正是名字所提供的东西——那个人不再是一个匿名的可能性。

senses.title: Settle a value or standard
senses.titleCN: 确定（数值、标准）：让它从此不再变
senses.definition: to establish a value or standard definitively
senses.definitionCN: 确定性地确立某一数值或标准
senses.example: The committee ascertained the minimum wage for the coming year.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会确定了来年的最低工资。
senses.why: Here the verb creates certainty rather than finding it: a decision fixes a standard. English uses ascertain in this legislative sense because the outcome is a settled figure.
senses.whyCN: 这里动词是在制造确定，而不是在发现确定：决定把一个标准固定下来。英语在这个立法意义上用 ascertain，因为结果是一个被定下的数。

senses.title: Make sure
senses.titleCN: 使确定、确保：古一点的“让某事成为定局”
senses.definition: (formal, older use) to make certain or ensure something
senses.definitionCN: （正式或较早用法）使某事确定或有保证
senses.example: The treaty was signed to ascertain the border between the two states.
senses.exampleCN: 条约的签署是为了确保两国之间的边界。
senses.why: This is the verb's oldest English layer, 'to make certain'. The modern 'find out' is a specialization: one way of making a thing certain is to establish it.
senses.whyCN: 这是动词最早的英语层次——“使确定”。现代的“查明”是一个专门化：让一件事确定的方式之一，就是把它确立起来。

senses.title: Tell someone for sure
senses.titleCN: （古）告知、保证：让对方心里有底
senses.definition: (obsolete) to inform someone or give them assurance
senses.definitionCN: （已废）告知某人或向其作出保证
senses.example: He ascertained them that the ship had arrived safely.
senses.exampleCN: 他向他们保证船已平安抵达。
senses.why: Early 15c. ascertain meant 'to inform, to give assurance', from Old French acertener 'to assure, certify'. The speaker makes the hearer certain; this sense is now obsolete and survives only in dictionaries.
senses.whyCN: 15 世纪初 ascertain 义为“告知、给予保证”，来自古法语 acertener“使确信、证明”。说话人让听者确定；这个义项现已废弃，只留在词典里。

intro.en: Ascertain begins as a French verb meaning 'to make sure', built from a- 'to' and certain, whose Latin base certus is literally 'sifted, decided'. English first used it for reassuring people, then narrowed it to finding facts out.
intro.cn: ascertain 起初是一个法语动词，义为“使确定”，由 a-“向”与 certain 构成，后者拉丁词基 certus 字面是“筛过的、定了的”。英语先用它表示让人安心，后来窄化为查明事实。

items.en: The root *krei- 'to sieve' is the reconstructed source of Latin cernere 'to sift, separate, decide'. No written PIE record survives, so this layer is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: 词根 *krei-“筛”是拉丁 cernere“筛、分开、判定”的重构来源。没有 PIE 书面记录留存，这一层标为“来源不确定”。

items.en: Latin certus 'determined, resolved, fixed, settled', originally a variant past participle of cernere, also meant 'placed beyond doubt, proved'. Its sense of a sifted residue becoming a decision is the seed of the whole family.
items.cn: 拉丁 certus“已定、已决、固定、确定”，原为 cernere 的变体过去分词，也义为“无可怀疑、已被证明”。筛剩下的东西成为决定，这一意象是整个词族的种子。

items.en: Vulgar Latin *certanus, an extended form of certus, gives Old French certain 'reliable, sure, assured'. The adjective is the base of the verb that follows.
items.cn: 俗拉丁 *certanus（certus 的扩展形式）给出古法语 certain“可靠的、确信的、有保证的”。这个形容词是随后动词的基础。

items.en: acertener 'to assure, certify' is formed with a- 'to' plus certain, literally 'to bring to a sure state'. Anglo-French acerteiner carries it across the Channel.
items.cn: acertener“使确信、证明”由 a-“向”加 certain 构成，字面即“带到确定状态”。英吉利法语 acerteiner 把它带过海峡。

items.en: Ascertain is recorded as 'to inform, to give assurance', a sense now obsolete. The speaker made the hearer certain rather than the speaker becoming certain himself.
items.cn: ascertain 记录为“告知、给予保证”，此义今已废弃。当时是说话人让听者确定，而不是说话人自己变得确定。

items.en: The meaning 'find out for sure by experiment or investigation' is attested by 1794, and ascertainable by 1765. The direction reverses: the mind now receives certainty from evidence rather than giving it to someone else.
items.cn: “通过实验或调查确实查明”义于 1794 年记录，ascertainable 于 1765 年出现。方向反了过来：心智现在从证据获得确定，而不是把确定给别人。

note.en: The first group is a trap: assert, ascetic and certain all sit near ascertain in spelling or sound, but only certain and certify share the cert- root. The second group gives the verbs that do the same work.
note.cn: 第一组是陷阱：assert、ascetic、certain 在拼写或读音上都靠近 ascertain，但只有 certain 与 certify 共享 cert- 词根。第二组才是做同一件事的动词。

entries.definition: to state firmly. From Latin asserere 'join to, claim', from serere 'join' — nothing to do with certus.
entries.definitionCN: 断言；坚称。来自拉丁 asserere“连接到、主张”，源自 serere“连接”，与 certus 无关。

entries.definition: practising severe self-discipline. From Greek askēsis 'exercise, training', not from Latin certus.
entries.definitionCN: 苦行的。来自希腊语 askēsis“锻炼、训练”，并非拉丁 certus。

entries.definition: sure, fixed; the adjective from which ascertain was built.
entries.definitionCN: 确定的；certain 正是构成 ascertain 的那个形容词。

entries.definition: to confirm formally in writing. Built on cert- plus -ify, it shares the 'made sure' core.
entries.definitionCN: 证明；核证。由 cert- 加 -ify 构成，共享“使确定”的核心。

entries.definition: to find out or decide something firmly, from Latin determinare 'set bounds to'.
entries.definitionCN: 确定；查明。来自拉丁 determinare“划定界限”。

entries.definition: to establish that something is true or accurate.
entries.definitionCN: 核实；证实某事真实或准确。

entries.definition: to establish the truth of something already believed or reported.
entries.definitionCN: 确认；证实已相信或已报告之事。

entries.definition: to prove or show something to be true beyond doubt.
entries.definitionCN: 确立；证实某事无可怀疑。

entries.definition: to find something previously unknown, often by chance or search.
entries.definitionCN: 发现；找到原先未知之物，常靠搜寻或偶然。

normalIntro.en: The word is a- plus certain: to ascertain is to bring something to the state of being certain. The sifting image of cernere sits inside certus.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 a- 加 certain：ascertain 就是把某物带到“确定”的状态。certus 里藏着 cernere 那把筛子。

normal.en: a- (to) + certain: to ascertain is to bring a matter to certainty.
normal.cn: a-（向）+ certain：ascertain 就是把一件事带到确定。

normal.en: cert- comes from cernere, 'to sift': what is ascertained is what remains after doubt is sifted away.
normal.cn: cert- 出自 cernere“筛”：被 ascertain 的，是疑点被筛掉后剩下的东西。

normal.en: ascertain is not assert: assert claims, ascertain checks.
normal.cn: ascertain 不是 assert：assert 是声称，ascertain 是核对。

normal.en: A surveyor ascertains a height; a court ascertains damages; both fix a figure.
normal.cn: 测量员 ascertain 高度，法庭 ascertain 损害赔偿；两者都是把一个数定下来。

normal.en: The old sense was 'to assure someone'; the modern one is 'to become sure yourself'.
normal.cn: 旧义是“向别人保证”，今义是“自己变得确定”。

abstract.en: Certainty is a residue: sift the claims and the fact is what is left.
abstract.cn: 确定是一种剩余物：把各种说法筛掉，剩下的事实才是确定的。

abstract.en: Measurement is decision with an instrument: the unknown becomes a quoted number.
abstract.cn: 测量是借助仪器的决定：未知之物变成一个可以被引用的数。

abstract.en: The word reverses direction over six centuries: from giving certainty to receiving it from evidence.
abstract.cn: 六个世纪里这个词换了方向：从把确定给别人，到从证据那里接受确定。

examples.en: Investigators are still trying to ascertain the cause of the fire.
examples.cn: 调查人员仍在努力查明火灾原因。

examples.en: Please ascertain whether the train leaves from platform three.
examples.cn: 请核实这趟列车是否从三号站台发车。

examples.en: The exact age of the rock was ascertained by radiocarbon dating.
examples.cn: 这块岩石的确切年龄是用放射性碳定年法测定的。

dict_mnemonic.note: 拆词联想 · 词源辅助
dict_mnemonic.text: a（向）+ certain（确定的）——把一件事带到“确定”的状态，就是“查明、弄清”；再往前一步，就是“使确定、确保”。

root: 源自古法语 acertener（a-“向”+ certain“确定的”）← 俗拉丁 *certanus ← 拉丁 certus“已定的、确定的”（原为 cernere“筛、分开、判定”的变体过去分词）；核心是“使确定、筛到只剩事实”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all circle one move: bringing something into a state of certainty. Sometimes that means sifting evidence, sometimes measuring a figure, sometimes naming a person, sometimes simply telling someone so.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项绕着同一个动作转：把某物带进“确定”的状态。有时是筛证据，有时是量出一个数，有时是点出一个人的名字，有时只是告诉别人让他放心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp-lit table where claims are crossed out one by one until a single line remains.
core.cn: 核心意象：灯下的一张桌子，说法被一条条划掉，只剩下一行。

branches.en: FINDING OUT: a fact sought by investigation, and a claim brought up against evidence.
branches.cn: 查明：以调查追出事实，以及把说法拿去与证据对证。

branches.en: FIXING A FIGURE: a quantity measured, and a standard settled by decision.
branches.cn: 定下一个数：被量出的量，以及由决定确立的标准。

branches.en: MAKING CERTAIN: a judgement reached by sifting, and the older sense of ensuring.
branches.cn: 使确定：筛出的判断，以及较早的“确保”义。

branches.en: PINNING A TARGET: an unknown person located and named.
branches.cn: 锁定目标：一个未知的人被定位并命名。

branches.en: THE OLD ASSURANCE: telling someone so that they may be certain.
branches.cn: 古老的保证：告诉别人，让他心里有底。

intro.en: Ascertain is a prefix plus an adjective turned verb: a- (from Latin ad-) plus certain. Its family grows with -able, -ment, -ty, -ly and the Latin cert- branch in certify and certificate.
intro.cn: ascertain 是前缀加“形容词转动词”：a-（来自拉丁 ad-）加 certain。词族再以 -able、-ment、-ty、-ly 生长，并在 certify、certificate 里延伸出拉丁 cert- 分支。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies certus and its source cernere 'to sift'. The a- is ad- reduced in French, and the -ain of certain is a French adjective ending, so the word reached English through French rather than directly from Rome.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供 certus 及其来源 cernere“筛”。a- 是法语中弱化的 ad-，certain 的 -ain 是法语形容词词尾，所以这个词是经法语进入英语的，不是直接从罗马来。

items.meaning: to bring to certainty; to find out
items.example: They ascertained the cause within a week.
items.exampleCN: 他们一周内查明了原因。

items.example: One thing is certain: the door was unlocked.
items.exampleCN: 有一点是确定的：门没锁。

items.example: We cannot speak with certainty about the motive.
items.exampleCN: 我们无法确定地说出动机。

items.example: The record certainly existed at some point.
items.exampleCN: 这份记录确实在某个时候存在过。

items.example: The cost is ascertainable from the invoices.
items.exampleCN: 费用可以从发票上查明。

items.example: The ascertainment of the facts took months.
items.exampleCN: 事实的查明花了几个月。

items.example: A doctor certified the cause of death.

items.meaning: a document that makes something certain
items.example: She showed a certificate of ownership.
He spoke with the certitude of a witness.
items.exampleCN: 他以证人的笃定口吻说话。

definition_zh: v. 把……归因于；把（作品、性质）归于某人名下
definition_en: To regard something as caused by a particular thing, or to name someone as the author or holder of a work or quality.
core_image: 在一行字旁边写下「这要记到那一项上」
scene: 他们把这场胜利归因于运气而非计划。They ascribe the win to luck rather than planning.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：ascribe 指把结果的原因归到某处，句式是 ascribe A to B。

collocations.zh: 把一首诗归于某人名下

senses.title: To name a cause
senses.definition: to regard an outcome as produced by a particular thing, in the pattern ascribe something to something
senses.definitionCN: 把某个结果看作由某事物造成，句式为 ascribe A to B
senses.example: Doctors ascribe the improvement to rest.
senses.exampleCN: 医生把好转归因于休息。
senses.why: The root means to write, so the word pictures writing a cause beside an entry, as a clerk would in a ledger.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为「写」，所以这个词画的是在一条记录旁写下原因，就像账房先生在账簿上做的那样。

senses.title: To name an author or holder
senses.definition: to say that a work, saying or quality belongs to a particular person, often with some doubt
senses.definitionCN: 说某件作品、说法或性质属于某人，常带有几分不确定
senses.example: The lines are ascribed to a later poet.
senses.exampleCN: 这几行诗被归于后世一位诗人名下。
senses.why: This sense keeps the ledger picture even more clearly: a name is written next to a work whose author is not certain.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项更清楚地保留了账簿画面：在作者并不确定的作品旁写上一个名字。

intro.en: Ascribe is Latin ascribere, from ad, to, plus scribere, to write: to write something in beside an entry, hence to assign it.
intro.cn: ascribe 就是拉丁语 ascribere，由 ad「向」加 scribere「写」构成：在某条记录旁写进去，因而引申为「归于」。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning to cut or scratch lies behind words for writing, since early writing was scratched.
items.cn: 一个拟构词根意为「切、划」，藏在众多与书写有关的词背后，因为早期文字是刻划出来的。

items.en: Latin scribere meant to write, and its participle scriptum gives script and scripture.
items.cn: 拉丁语 scribere 意为「写」，其分词 scriptum 产生 script 与 scripture。

items.en: With ad, to, ascribere meant to write in addition, to enter a name on a list.
items.cn: 加上 ad「向」之后，ascribere 意为「附加写上」，即把名字登记入册。

items.en: The noun ascriptio named that act of entering something beside an entry.
items.cn: 名词 ascriptio 指那种在某条记录旁登记的行为。

items.en: English took ascribe in the fifteenth century, at first of enrolling people and later of assigning causes.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入 ascribe，起初指登记入册，后来指归派原因。

items.en: Scholarship then used the verb for works whose author was uncertain, a use still common in textual study.
items.cn: 此后学界用这个动词指作者不确定的作品，这一用法在文本研究中至今仍常见。

note.en: The look-alike group is a full lesson in the writing root; the near-meaning group separates neutral cause from praise and from blame.
note.cn: 形近组是一堂完整的「写」词根课；近义组把中性的归因与「归功」和「归罪」区分开。

entries.definition: To say what something is like.
To write or carve words on a surface.
To sign up to receive or support something.
To lay down a rule or order a medicine.
To regard something as caused by a thing.
entries.definitionCN: 把某事看作由某物造成。

entries.definition: To give something to a person or class.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物派给某人或某类。

entries.definition: To hold someone responsible for something good.
To lay a fault or blame on someone.
entries.definitionCN: 把过错或罪责归到某人身上。

normalIntro.en: Ascribe is ad, to, plus scribere, write: writing a cause or a name beside a thing.
normalIntro.cn: ascribe 就是 ad「向」加 scribere「写」：在事物旁边写下一个原因或一个名字。

normal.en: The pattern is ascribe something to something.
normal.cn: 句式是 ascribe A to B。

normal.en: Describe, inscribe and subscribe share the root.
normal.cn: describe、inscribe、subscribe 共用这个词根。

normal.en: Ascription is the noun, ascribable the adjective.
normal.cn: ascription 是名词，ascribable 是形容词。

normal.en: Attribute is the everyday substitute.
normal.cn: attribute 是日常替换词。

normal.en: Impute adds blame, credit adds praise.
normal.cn: impute 带责难，credit 带褒奖。

abstract.en: Picture a clerk writing a reason in a margin.
abstract.cn: 想象账房在页边写下一个理由。

abstract.en: Imagine a name added beside an unsigned poem.
abstract.cn: 想象一首无署名诗旁被添上一个名字。

abstract.en: Think of an arrow drawn from result to cause.
abstract.cn: 想象一支从结果指向原因的箭头。

examples.en: She ascribed her calm to long practice.
examples.cn: 她把自己的镇静归因于长期练习。

examples.en: The error was ascribed to a faulty sensor.
examples.cn: 这次误差被归因于一个失灵传感器。

examples.en: Critics ascribe the play to two authors.
examples.cn: 评论者把这出戏归于两位作者名下。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：a-「向」+ scribe「写」——在旁边写上一笔「这归它」，就是 ascribe「归因于」。

root: 拉丁语 scribere「写」加 ad-「向」构成 ascribere「附加登记」，名词 ascriptio 随之而来；十五世纪入英语，由「登记入册」引申为「归因、归于名下」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses write something beside something else: a cause beside a result, or a name beside a work of uncertain authorship.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都是「在旁边写上一笔」：在结果旁写原因，或在作者不明的作品旁写名字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a note written beside an entry saying this belongs there
core.cn: 核心意象：在一行字旁写下「这要记到那一项上」

branches.en: A win written down to luck.
Lines placed under a later poet.
branches.cn: 把诗句归到后世诗人名下。

branches.en: A play claimed for two authors.
branches.cn: 把一出戏说成两位作者所作。

branches.en: Both add a note beside the thing itself.
branches.cn: 两者都在事物本身旁添上一笔。

intro.en: Ascribe is a- from ad- plus -scribe, write; the same root fills describe, inscribe, subscribe, prescribe and script.
intro.cn: ascribe 由 ad- 变来的 a- 加 -scribe「写」构成；同一词根填满 describe、inscribe、subscribe、prescribe 与 script。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is scribere, to write, ascribere, to write in beside, and scriptum, a thing written.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 scribere「写」、ascribere「旁注登记」与 scriptum「写下之物」。

latinEntries.meaning: to write in beside, to enrol

latinEntries.exampleCN: scriptum 产生 script 与 scripture。

definition_zh: 灰；灰烬；白蜡树
definition_en: the grey powder left after something burns, or a tall tree with hard pale wood
core_image: 火熄之后，灶底剩下一层细白的灰
scene: 壁炉里的木柴烧了整夜，早上只剩下粉末。The fire had left a layer of ash on the stones.
sceneCN: 这里 ash 是「灰烬」（第 1 个义项：燃烧后剩下的粉末）；句意是炉火在石面上留下了一层灰。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：覆着灰的；灰似的

senses.title: Powder left by fire
senses.definition: the soft grey remains of something that has burned
senses.definitionCN: 某物燃烧后留下的松软灰色残余
senses.example: The fire had left a layer of ash on the stones.
senses.exampleCN: 炉火在石面上留下了一层灰。
senses.why: Old English asce named the burnt powder, and the word has kept that sense for a thousand years.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 asce 指燃烧后的粉末，这个词一千年来都保留着这一义。

senses.title: A tall hardwood tree
senses.definition: a tree with pale strong wood and winged seeds
senses.definitionCN: 木质浅色坚硬、结翅果的高大树木
senses.example: An old ash stands at the corner of the field.
senses.exampleCN: 田地角上立着一棵老白蜡树。
senses.why: This is a different Old English word, aesc, which happened to fall together in spelling and sound.
senses.whyCN: 这其实是另一个古英语词 aesc，只是拼写与读音后来与「灰」合流了。

intro.en: Ash joins two Old English words that came to look alike.
intro.cn: ash 合并了两个原本不同、后来形貌相近的古英语词。

items.en: asce meant 'ash, burnt powder'.
items.cn: asce 意为「灰、燃烧后的粉末」。

items.en: aesc meant 'ash tree' and also named the rune for it.
items.cn: aesc 意为「白蜡树」，也指代表它的卢恩字母。

items.en: Both words settled into the spelling asshe.
items.cn: 两个词都归入拼写 asshe。

items.en: The modern spelling ash became standard.
items.cn: 现代拼写 ash 成为标准。

items.en: The tree sense survives mainly in wood and plant names.
items.cn: 树木义主要保留在木材与植物名称中。

note.en: The look-alike group is the ash family; the near-meaning group gives other burnt remains.
note.cn: 形近组是 ash 词族；近义组是其他燃烧残余。

entries.definition: burnt remains, plural
pale grey
covered with ash
a partly burnt piece
black powder from smoke
a glowing piece of coal

normalIntro.en: Ash is what fire leaves behind.
normalIntro.cn: ash 就是火留下的东西。

normal.en: The burnt sense is usually uncountable.
normal.cn: 「灰烬」义通常不可数。

normal.en: Ashes in the plural can mean a person's remains.
normal.cn: 复数 ashes 可指人的骨灰。

normal.en: The tree sense survives in ash wood.
normal.cn: 树木义保留在「白蜡木」这类说法里。

normal.en: Ash blonde describes a pale hair colour.
normal.cn: ash blonde 形容浅灰金色的头发。

normal.en: The word is one short syllable: ASH.
normal.cn: 这个词只有一个短音节：ASH。

abstract.en: See grey flakes settling in a fireplace.
abstract.cn: 想象灰色薄片落在壁炉里。

abstract.en: See a pale trunk with winged seeds.
abstract.cn: 想象浅色树干与翅果。

abstract.en: See a cigarette tip drop grey dust.
abstract.cn: 想象烟头落下灰色粉末。

examples.en: The fire had left a layer of ash on the stones.
examples.cn: 炉火在石面上留下了一层灰。

examples.en: An old ash stands at the corner of the field.
examples.cn: 田地角上立着一棵老白蜡树。

examples.en: Volcanic ash covered the roofs of the village.
examples.cn: 火山灰盖住了村子的屋顶。

dict_mnemonic.text: ash 有两个来源：烧完的灰，和长着浅色木头的白蜡树，拼写相同而已。

root: 一词合两源：灰烬义来自古英语 asce；白蜡树义来自古英语 aesc，兼指对应卢恩字母。二者后世同形同音。

sensesIntro.en: Fire leaves a powder, and a field may hold a tree whose name looks the same.
sensesIntro.cn: 火留下粉末，田野里也可能立着一棵名字形貌相同的树。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin grey layer where a fire burned out.
core.cn: 核心意象：火烧尽之处留下的薄薄灰层。

intro.en: A short Germanic word with very little compounding.
intro.cn: 这是一个简短的日耳曼词，复合形式很少。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is native English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，是英语本族词。

definition_zh: 方面；外观；朝向
definition_en: one part of a situation, the look of something, or the direction a place faces
core_image: 同一件东西从不同角度看，显出不同的面
scene: 报告只写了成本，没提对居民的影响。The report ignores the human aspect of the change.
sceneCN: 这里 aspect 是「方面」（第 1 个义项：整体中的一个侧面）；句意是报告忽略了这一变化涉及人的方面。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：方面的；（语法）体的

senses.title: One side of a matter
senses.definition: a particular part of a larger situation or subject
senses.definitionCN: 较大情况或主题中的一个特定部分
senses.example: The report ignores the human aspect of the change.
senses.exampleCN: 报告忽略了这一变化涉及人的方面。
senses.why: Latin aspicere meant 'to look at'; the aspect is what a matter looks like from one direction.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 aspicere 意为「看」；aspect 就是一件事从某个方向看过去的样子。

senses.title: The look of something
senses.definition: the appearance a thing presents
senses.definitionCN: 事物呈现出来的外貌
senses.example: The house took on a gloomy aspect in the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 雨中这房子显得阴沉。
senses.why: Since aspect is what is seen, it can name the visible face of a place or a face itself.
senses.whyCN: 既然 aspect 是被看见的东西，它就能指一个地方或一张面孔可见的样子。

senses.title: The direction something faces
senses.definition: the way a building or slope faces
senses.definitionCN: 建筑物或坡面所朝的方向
senses.example: A southern aspect keeps the garden warm.
senses.exampleCN: 朝南的朝向让花园保持温暖。
senses.why: The direction from which a place is viewed also decides how much light it receives, hence the compass sense.
senses.whyCN: 一个地方被观看的方向也决定它受多少光，于是产生表示方位的用法。

intro.en: Aspect comes from a Latin verb meaning 'to look at'.
intro.cn: aspect 来自一个意为「看」的拉丁动词。

items.en: specere meant 'to look, to see'.
items.cn: specere 意为「看、看见」。

items.en: ad plus specere meant 'to look toward'.
items.cn: ad 与 specere 结合，意为「朝……看」。

items.en: aspectus meant 'a look, an appearance'.
items.cn: aspectus 意为「目光、外观」。

items.en: English aspect first meant the look of a face or sky.
items.cn: 英语 aspect 最初指面孔或天空的样子。

items.en: The word widened to any side of a question.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到问题的任何一个侧面。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the spect root; the near-meaning group gives feature, side, and view.
note.cn: 形近组保留 spect 词根；近义组给出 feature、side 与 view。

entries.definition: sides, plural
relating to aspect
in aspect terms
a noticeable part
one part of a matter
a way of seeing something

normalIntro.en: An aspect is one face of a many-sided thing.
normalIntro.cn: aspect 就是多面之物的一面。

normal.en: An aspect of is the usual pattern.
normal.cn: an aspect of 是最常见的搭配。

normal.en: In grammar, aspect marks how an action unfolds.
normal.cn: 语法里，aspect 表示动作的进行方式。

normal.en: The compas sense survives in estate writing.
normal.cn: 方位义仍见于房产描述文字。

normal.en: The plural is aspects.
normal.cn: 复数是 aspects。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AS-pect.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AS-pect。

abstract.en: See a cube turned to show one face.
abstract.cn: 想象立方体转动，露出一面。

abstract.en: See a window facing south light.
abstract.cn: 想象朝南接光的窗。

abstract.en: See the same event from two balconies.
abstract.cn: 想象从两个阳台看同一件事。

examples.en: The report ignores the human aspect of the change.
examples.cn: 报告忽略了这一变化涉及人的方面。

examples.en: The house took on a gloomy aspect in the rain.
examples.cn: 雨中这房子显得阴沉。

examples.en: A southern aspect keeps the garden warm.
examples.cn: 朝南的朝向让花园保持温暖。

dict_mnemonic.text: a-（向）加 spect（看）：朝某个方向看过去所见的那一面，就是一个方面。

root: 来自拉丁语 aspectus「外观、目光」，源自动词 aspicere「朝……看」，由 ad 与 specere「看」构成；由「所见之面」引申为方面与朝向。

sensesIntro.en: What you see from one side is a face, a look, or a direction.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一侧看见的东西，可以是一面、一种外观，也可以是一个朝向。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cube turned so one face catches the light.
core.cn: 核心意象：立方体转动，一面接住光。

intro.en: A Latin noun of looking that English turned toward ideas.
intro.cn: 这是一个拉丁语「观看」名词，英语把它转向了抽象观念。

latinIntro.en: The root specere also gives inspect, respect, and spectator.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 specere 也派生出 inspect、respect 与 spectator。

definition_zh: 志向；渴望达到的目标；送气发音；吸入；抽吸；一丝气息
definition_en: a strong hope or aim to achieve something, or the act of breathing something in
core_image: 一个人站在海边深吸一口气，眼睛望着对岸还看不见的灯光
scene: 她把想去对岸读书的念头写在信的末尾，写完又对着窗外深吸了一口气。Her aspiration to study abroad survived two failed applications.
sceneCN: 这里 aspiration 指「想要达到的目标与渴望」（第 1 个义项：志向上的愿望）；句意为她想出国读书的志向挺过了两次申请失败。图中可辨识物件：写满字的信纸、窗外对岸的灯光、被吸进胸腔的一口气、两次退回的信封。

pos.zh: 志向；渴望；送气音；吸入；抽吸

derivatives.zh: 基础动词，来自拉丁语「向某处呼气」，语义为「渴望、立志」
由名词加形容词后缀构成，语义由「志向」转为「以志向为标榜的」
由过去分词转为形容词，语义由「送气」转为「带送气的」
由动词词干加表示人的后缀构成，语义由「渴望」转为「追求某职位的人」

senses.title: A hoped-for aim
senses.definition: a strong hope or ambition to achieve something in the future
senses.definitionCN: 对未来取得某物所抱的强烈希望或志向
senses.example: Her aspiration to study abroad survived two failed applications.
senses.exampleCN: 她想出国读书的志向挺过了两次申请失败。
senses.why: the Latin verb meant to breathe toward something, so an aspiration is a breath aimed at a distant object.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁动词意为「朝某物呼气」，因此志向就是一缕朝远处目标呼出的气。

senses.title: Longing for high rank
senses.titleCN: 对高位或大成就的渴望
senses.definition: a desire for a high position, honour or a distinguished place
senses.definitionCN: 对高职位、荣誉或显要位置的渴求
senses.example: His aspiration to the chair was known to everyone but him.
senses.exampleCN: 他想坐主席位子的心思，除了他自己，人人都知道。
senses.why: breathing toward a seat of honour is the social form of the same reach.
senses.whyCN: 朝着荣誉之位呼一口气，是同一份伸手在社会层面的形态。

senses.title: Breath released in speech
senses.definition: the audible burst of breath that follows some consonants, as in the p of pin
senses.definitionCN: 某些辅音之后可听见的一股气流，如某些词首那个辅音之后的气
senses.example: The teacher marked the aspiration after the t with a small hook.
senses.exampleCN: 老师在那个辅音之后用一个小钩标出送气。
senses.why: the phonetic sense is the literal one: breath pushed out at the moment of speaking.
senses.whyCN: 语音义是最字面的用法：说话那一刻把气推出来。

senses.title: Drawing foreign matter into the lungs
senses.definition: the entry of food, liquid or other matter into the airway and lungs
senses.definitionCN: 食物、液体或其他物质进入气道与肺部
senses.example: The nurse watched for aspiration during the night feed.
senses.exampleCN: 夜间喂食时护士一直留意有无误吸。
senses.why: here breathing in becomes dangerous because what is drawn in does not belong in the lungs.
senses.whyCN: 这里的「吸」变得危险，因为被吸进去的东西不该在肺里。

senses.title: Removal by suction
senses.definition: the use of suction to draw fluid or tissue out of a cavity
senses.definitionCN: 用负压把液体或组织从腔体中吸出
senses.example: The aspiration of the cyst took less than a minute.
senses.exampleCN: 囊肿的抽吸不到一分钟就完成了。
senses.why: the same drawing motion is turned to medical use, where breath is replaced by a pump.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「吸」的动作被转作医疗用途，只是呼气换成了泵。

senses.title: Drawing fluid up a tube
senses.definition: the lifting of liquid by reduced pressure in an engine, pump or laboratory line
senses.definitionCN: 在发动机、泵或实验管路中借压差把液体吸上来
senses.example: Fuel aspiration failed when the line cracked.
senses.exampleCN: 管路开裂后燃油抽吸失效。
senses.why: machines borrow the word because a pump also pulls matter toward itself by creating a void.
senses.whyCN: 机器借用这个词，因为泵也靠制造空处把物质拉向自己。

senses.title: A breath of air
senses.definition: a single breath or a faint movement of air
senses.definitionCN: 一次呼吸，或空气极轻微的流动
senses.example: An aspiration of wind came through the shutter and moved the ash.
senses.exampleCN: 一丝风从百叶窗里进来，吹动了灰。
senses.why: the oldest physical layer survives in literary use, where the word means the air itself.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的物理层在文学用法里留存，那里这个词指空气本身。

senses.title: Shared hopes of a group
senses.definition: the collective hopes that a community or a generation holds for its future
senses.definitionCN: 一个社群或一代人对自身未来所抱的共同希望
senses.example: The school was built on the aspirations of families who had never had one.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校建立于那些从未有过学校的家庭的期盼之上。
senses.why: many breaths aimed at one future add up to a public aspiration, which is how politics uses the word.
senses.whyCN: 许多口气朝同一个未来呼出，就汇成一种公共期盼，政治语言正是这样用它的。

intro.en: Aspiration comes from Latin aspiratio 'a breathing upon', from aspirare 'to breathe toward', built on ad- 'to' and spirare 'to breathe'. The deeper origin of spirare is not settled. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 该词来自拉丁 aspiratio「朝某物呼气」，其动词 aspirare「向……呼气」由 ad-「向」与 spirare「呼吸」构成。spirare 的更深来源尚无定论，年代均为约数。

items.en: Spirare meant 'to breathe, to blow'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the comparison with a root for 'to blow' is a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: spirare 意为「呼吸、吹」。其更深来源不确定；把它与表示「吹」的词根相比对，只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus spirare gave aspirare 'to breathe upon, to blow toward', and by metaphor to favour or to strive toward.
items.cn: ad-「向」加 spirare 构成 aspirare「朝……呼气、向……吹」，并比喻为「眷顾」或「向往」。

items.en: The noun aspiratio named the breathing and, in grammar, the rough breathing marked over certain letters.
items.cn: 名词 aspiratio 指这股呼气，并在语法中指标在某些字母上的粗气符号。

items.en: English took the noun in the fourteenth century, first for the grammatical sense of rough breathing.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪吸收了这个名词，最早用于语法上的「粗气」义。

items.en: From the sixteenth century the word was used for a hope directed at a high aim, and the medical suction sense followed in the nineteenth.
items.cn: 从十六世纪起，这个词用于指向高目标的希望；医学上的抽吸义在十九世纪随后出现。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin of spirare and the dating of the hopeful sense): no citation fixes the first use for ambition, and any Indo-European form offered for spirare is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（spirare 的更深来源与希望义的确切年代）：没有书证能定住它首次用于「抱负」的时间；凡为 spirare 给出的印欧语形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one separates look-alikes built on the breathing verb from words that only sound similar; group two separates kinds of longing.
note.cn: 第一组区分同出「呼吸」动词的形近词与只是读音相近的词；第二组区分不同类型的渴望。

entries.definition: To aim at something high; the noun is the state, the verb is the reaching.
entries.definitionCN: 朝高处立志；名词是那个状态，动词是那次伸手。

entries.definition: In- 'into' plus spirare: a breathing in, hence the sudden idea that seems to arrive from outside.
entries.definitionCN: 由 in-「入」加 spirare 构成：吸进来，因而指仿佛从外面到来的灵感。

entries.definition: Ex- 'out' plus spirare: breathing out, and by extension the end of a period when time has run out.
entries.definitionCN: 由 ex-「出」加 spirare 构成：呼出，并引申指期限走完的到期。

entries.definition: Re- 'again' plus spirare: the whole cycle of breathing, with no aim attached.
entries.definitionCN: 由 re-「再」加 spirare 构成：整个呼吸循环，不含目标。

entries.definition: From the same sprinkling verb, but it means a casting of doubt or a slander, not a hope.
entries.definitionCN: 同出那个「洒、喷」的动词，但意思是对人泼脏水、造谣中伤，而非希望。

entries.definition: A strong desire to rise in status or power; it is more worldly than aspiration.
entries.definitionCN: 对地位或权力上升的强烈欲望；比 aspiration 更世俗。

entries.definition: A specific end point one works toward; it is the target itself, not the longing for it.
entries.definitionCN: 努力所指向的具体终点；是目标本身，而不是对目标的渴望。

entries.definition: A cherished wish, often distant and not yet planned; it is warmer and looser than aspiration.
entries.definitionCN: 珍爱的愿望，往往遥远且尚无计划；比 aspiration 更温暖也更松散。

entries.definition: A deep and often painful longing; it stresses the ache rather than the plan to achieve.
entries.definitionCN: 深沉而常带痛感的渴望；强调那份渴，而不是实现它的计划。

entries.definition: The amount taken into the body or a machine in a period; it is the plain physical relative of the suction sense.
entries.definitionCN: 一段时间内进入身体或机器的量；是抽吸义最朴素的物理近亲。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The Latin verb means to breathe toward something, so a strong hope is a breath aimed at a far target.
normal.cn: 那个拉丁动词意为「朝某物呼气」，因此一份强烈的希望就是一缕朝远处目标呼出的气。

normal.en: The family runs aspire, aspiration, aspirant, aspirational, aspirated.
normal.cn: 同族词覆盖动词、名词、追求者、愿景式形容词与送气形容词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: career aspirations, aspiration pneumonia, aspirated consonant.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：职业志向、吸入性肺炎、送气辅音。

normal.en: The same breathing verb gives inspiration, expiration and respiration, each with its own prefix direction.
normal.cn: 同一个「呼吸」动词还给出 inspiration、expiration 与 respiration，各自带有自己的前缀方向。

normal.en: Medical suction keeps the physical picture: something is drawn out of a cavity by reduced pressure.
normal.cn: 医学抽吸保留了物理图景：靠压差把某物从腔体中吸出。

abstract.en: Picture a long breath held while looking across water at lights not yet reachable.
abstract.cn: 想象隔水望着还够不到的灯光时，长长地屏住一口气。

abstract.en: Picture a seed on a sill, leaning toward a window it cannot move to.
abstract.cn: 想象窗台上的一粒种子，朝它无法移动过去的窗子倾斜。

abstract.en: Picture a letter written and rewritten but never sent, kept in a drawer.
abstract.cn: 想象一封写了又改、始终没寄出的信，放在抽屉里。

examples.en: The scholarship matched her aspiration with a place at the college.
examples.cn: 这笔奖学金让她的志向与一个学院名额对上了。

examples.en: Rural families spoke of their aspirations for a clinic of their own.
examples.cn: 乡下家庭谈起他们想要一所自己的诊所的期盼。

examples.en: The doctor ordered suction to prevent aspiration during sleep.
examples.cn: 医生安排了吸痰，以防睡眠中误吸。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「a 斯匹瑞」——朝远处深吸一口气再向前望 → 志向、渴望

root: 拉丁 aspiratio「呼气」← aspirare「向……呼气」= ad-（向）+ spirare（呼吸）；spirare 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one breath: air is aimed at a far object and becomes a hope; the same air is aimed at a seat of honour, then at a consonant, then drawn into a lung, then pulled by a pump, then felt as a faint wind, and finally shared by a whole community.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一口气展开：气朝远处目标呼出而成希望；同一口气再朝荣誉之位、朝一个辅音、进一只肺、被泵抽动、化作一丝风，最后被整个社群共同呼出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long breath drawn at the shore while looking at lights across the water.
core.cn: 核心意象：站在岸边望着对岸的灯光，长长吸一口气。

branches.en: THE BREATH AIMED HIGH: hope for an aim and hunger for a seat of honour.
branches.cn: 朝高处呼出的气：对目标的希望，以及对荣誉之位的渴求。

branches.en: THE BREATH HEARD: phonetics keeps the literal push of air.
branches.cn: 被听见的气：语音学保留了最字面的推气。

branches.en: MATTER DRAWN IN: what enters a lung and what a pump pulls up a line.
branches.cn: 被吸进的物质：进入肺里的东西，与泵沿着管路抽上来的东西。

branches.en: MATTER TAKEN OUT: clinical suction reverses the direction and removes.
branches.cn: 被取出的物质：临床抽吸把方向反过来，取走东西。

branches.en: FROM A GUST TO A GENERATION: one faint breath widens into the shared hopes of many.
branches.cn: 从一阵微风到一代人：一丝微弱的气，扩展成许多人的共同期盼。

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb plus a noun suffix, and the same prefix and verb build several common English words, so the family is easy to read by parts.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个拉丁动词加名词后缀，同一个前缀与动词还构成若干常用英语词，因此这一族很容易按部件读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin spirare 'to breathe' gives spirit, inspire, expire, respire and conspire; ad- 'to' appears in adapt, adjacent and admire.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 spirare「呼吸」衍生出 spirit、inspire、expire、respire 与 conspire；ad-「向」见于 adapt、adjacent 与 admire。

items.example: The prefix points the breath at an object.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把气指向某个对象。
这个词根带着呼吸这个动作。

items.example: The wind seemed to strive toward the cliff.
items.exampleCN: 那阵风仿佛朝崖上使劲。

items.example: Her aspiration was to build a clinic.
items.exampleCN: 她的志向是建一所诊所。

items.structure: aspirare passing into French and English
items.example: He aspired to the vacant chair.
items.exampleCN: 他渴望那把空出的椅子。
十名求职者参加了考试。

items.example: The poster was aspirational rather than factual.
items.exampleCN: 这张海报是励志的，而不是写实的。

items.meaning: pronounced with a burst of breath
items.example: The aspirated consonant was hard for the children.
items.exampleCN: 这个送气辅音让孩子们觉得难。

items.meaning: a breathing in, a sudden idea
items.example: The design came in a single inspiration.
items.exampleCN: 这个设计来自一次顿悟。

items.meaning: breathing out, the end of a term
items.example: The lease reached expiration in June.
The spirit of the place was quiet.
items.exampleCN: 这个地方的气息很安静。

definition_zh: 立志；渴望达到；谋求职位；向往
definition_en: to desire strongly to achieve something high or to become a certain kind of person
core_image: 一个孩子趴在窗台上，看远处塔楼的尖顶，一直看到脖子发酸
scene: 她十六岁那年看完一本关于深海的书，从此决定要做海洋生物学家。She aspired to study the deep sea years before any university had replied.
sceneCN: 这里 aspire 指「立志要达到某个高目标」（第 1 个义项：朝高处立志）；句意为在还没有任何大学回信之前，她早已立志研究深海。图中可辨识物件：远处的塔尖、被翻旧的深海书、窗台的手印、尚未拆封的回信。

pos.zh: 立志；渴望（与 to、after 搭配）

derivatives.zh: 由动词加表示行为的名词后缀构成，语义由「朝高处呼气」转为「志向」
由动词词干加表示人的后缀构成，语义由「渴望」转为「谋求者」
由现在分词转为形容词，语义由「正立志」转为「有志于进入某行的」
由名词加形容词后缀构成，语义由「志向」转为「带有志向色彩的、励志的」

senses.title: Aim at a distant goal
senses.definition: to set one's hopes on a goal that lies well beyond present reach
senses.definitionCN: 把希望放在一个远超出当下能力所及的目标上
senses.example: She aspired to study the deep sea long before any university had replied.
senses.exampleCN: 在还没有任何大学回信之前，她早已立志研究深海。
senses.why: the Latin verb means to breathe toward something, so aspiring is aiming one's whole breath at a far object.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁动词意为「朝某物呼气」，因此立志就是把整口气都朝一个远处的对象呼去。

senses.title: Seek a particular office
senses.definition: to try to obtain a post, title or place that others may also want
senses.definitionCN: 试图取得一个别人也想要的职位、头衔或位子
senses.example: Three deputies aspired to the vacant chair.
senses.exampleCN: 三位副手都想坐上那把空出的椅子。
senses.why: the Roman picture was a candidate walking around to court votes, and that political sense never left the word.
senses.whyCN: 罗马的图景是候选人四处奔走拉票，那层政治意味从未离开这个词。

senses.title: Want to become a certain person
senses.definition: to wish to turn oneself into a particular kind of person or worker
senses.definitionCN: 希望把自己变成某一类人或某一种从业者
senses.example: He aspired to be a country doctor rather than a famous surgeon.
senses.exampleCN: 他想做乡村医生，而不是名医。
senses.why: the aim is no longer a thing but an identity, and the same upward breath is directed at a self to be built.
senses.whyCN: 目标不再是一件东西，而是一种身份，同一口向上的气被呼向一个待建成的自己。

senses.title: Emulate a standard
senses.definition: to measure oneself against a model or a standard set by others
senses.definitionCN: 拿自己与别人立下的榜样或标准相比照
senses.example: Her early drawings aspired to the plainness of the old masters.
senses.exampleCN: 她早期的素描向往古代大师那种朴素。
senses.why: breathing toward a model is how skill is acquired: one imitates before one can invent.
senses.whyCN: 朝榜样呼气正是技艺获得的途径：先模仿，才谈得上创造。

senses.title: Hope for an ideal condition
senses.definition: to long for a better condition such as peace, fairness or quiet
senses.definitionCN: 渴望更好的处境，如和平、公平或安宁
senses.example: The whole valley aspired to nothing more than a quiet winter.
senses.exampleCN: 整个山谷向往的不过是一个安静的冬天。
senses.why: the object can be a condition rather than a possession, which is why the word suits public hopes.
senses.whyCN: 对象可以是一种处境而非一件所有物，因此这个词适合表达公共的希望。

senses.title: Rise physically
senses.definition: to rise or tower upward, said of buildings, smoke or terrain in older prose
senses.definitionCN: 向上升起或高耸，旧时用于建筑、烟或地形
senses.example: The spire aspired so high that the bells could be heard across the river.
senses.exampleCN: 那尖顶高耸，钟声在河对岸都听得见。
senses.why: this is the plain physical sense of breathing upward, before the word was narrowed to desire.
senses.whyCN: 这是「向上呼气」最朴素的物理义，出现在词义收窄为「渴望」之前。

senses.title: Pronounce with a breath
senses.definition: to utter a consonant with a audible puff of breath, as in the p of pin
senses.definitionCN: 发音时带出一股听得见的气，如某些词里那个辅音之后的气
senses.example: In this dialect speakers aspire the t at the end of a word.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个方言里，说话人会把词尾那个辅音发成送气音。
senses.why: phonetics kept the literal meaning, since the sound really is a breath pushed out.
senses.whyCN: 语音学保留了字面意思，因为那个音确实就是被推出来的一口气。

senses.title: Long for something intensely
senses.definition: to desire something intensely, often used with after in formal prose
senses.definitionCN: 强烈地想要某物，正式文字中后面常接一个介词
senses.example: The exiled poet aspired after one more sight of the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 流亡的诗人心心念念再看一眼那些山。
senses.why: when the object is out of reach, the verb carries pure longing rather than a plan.
senses.whyCN: 当对象无法到手，这个动词就带着纯粹的渴，而不是一份计划。

intro.en: Aspire comes from Latin aspirare 'to breathe upon, to blow toward', built on ad- 'to' and spirare 'to breathe'. The deeper origin of spirare is not settled. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 该词来自拉丁 aspirare「朝……呼气、向……吹」，由 ad-「向」与 spirare「呼吸」构成。spirare 的更深来源尚无定论，年代均为约数。

items.en: Spirare meant 'to breathe, to blow'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the tie proposed to a root for 'to blow' is a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: spirare 意为「呼吸、吹」。其更深来源不确定；把它与表示「吹」的词根相联系，只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus spirare gave aspirare 'to breathe upon', and metaphorically to favour someone or to strive toward something.
items.cn: ad-「向」加 spirare 构成 aspirare「朝……呼气」，并比喻为「眷顾某人」或「向往某物」。

items.en: Roman writers used the verb for courting support, so the word entered English with a political edge before it meant plain longing.
items.cn: 罗马作家用这个动词表示争取支持，因此这个词带着政治色彩进入英语，早于它表示单纯渴望。

items.en: English took the verb in the fourteenth century, at first in the sense of rising or towering, then of hoping for high things.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪吸收了这个动词，先表「升起、高耸」，再表「向往高处之物」。

items.en: Grammarians applied the same word to consonants pronounced with breath, which is the oldest physical layer kept in technical use.
items.cn: 语法学家把同一个词用于带气发音的辅音，这是最古老的物理层在技术用语中的保存。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin of spirare and the dating of the hopeful sense): no citation fixes when rising became longing, and any Indo-European form offered for spirare is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（spirare 的更深来源与希望义的确切年代）：没有书证能定住「升起」何时变成「渴望」；凡为 spirare 给出的印欧语形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one separates words built on the same breathing verb; group two separates verbs of wanting by how reachable the object is.
note.cn: 第一组区分同出「呼吸」动词的词；第二组按对象的可达程度区分表示「想要」的动词。

entries.definition: In- 'into' plus spirare: to breathe a feeling into someone, hence to fill them with enthusiasm.
entries.definitionCN: 由 in-「入」加 spirare 构成：把某种感受吹进别人心里，因而指激发热情。

entries.definition: Ex- 'out' plus spirare: to breathe out one's last breath, hence to come to an end.
entries.definitionCN: 由 ex-「出」加 spirare 构成：呼出最后一口气，因而指终了、到期。

entries.definition: Com- 'together' plus spirare: to breathe as one, hence to plot together in secret.
entries.definitionCN: 由 com-「共同」加 spirare 构成：同呼一口气，因而指暗中合谋。

entries.definition: Per- 'through' plus spirare: to breathe through the skin, that is, to sweat.
entries.definitionCN: 由 per-「穿过」加 spirare 构成：透过皮肤呼气，也就是出汗。

entries.definition: From Latin asper 'rough': harshness of surface or manner, with no connection to breathing.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 asper「粗糙」：表面或态度的粗硬，与呼吸无关。

entries.definition: To want something with a real chance in view; it can be modest, while aspiring is always aimed high.
entries.definitionCN: 在还看得见机会的情况下想要某事；可以很小，而立志总是朝高处。

entries.definition: To want something, often without any plan to get it; it carries no effort.
entries.definitionCN: 想要某物，往往没有任何获取的计划；不含努力。

entries.definition: To feel a deep and often painful desire; the feeling outweighs the aim.
entries.definitionCN: 怀着深沉而常带痛的渴望；感受压过了目标。

entries.definition: To try actively to find or obtain something; it names the activity rather than the ambition.
entries.definitionCN: 积极地设法找到或取得；指活动，而不是抱负。

entries.definition: To struggle hard toward something; it stresses the exertion, while aspire stresses the height of the aim.
entries.definitionCN: 奋力朝某处挣扎；强调使力，而 aspire 强调目标的高度。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Ad- 'to' plus spirare 'breathe': to breathe toward something far away.
normal.cn: ad-「向」加 spirare「呼吸」：朝远处某物呼出一口气。

normal.en: The family runs aspire, aspiration, aspirant, aspiring, aspirational.
normal.cn: 同族词覆盖动词、名词、谋求者、现在分词形容词与励志形容词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the objects: aspire to a post, aspire to become, aspire after honour.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出对象：谋求职位、渴望成为、渴求荣誉。

normal.en: The political origin survives in aspirant, the person who wants the seat.
normal.cn: 政治来源仍活在「谋求者」这个名词里，指那个想要位子的人。

normal.en: Phonetics keeps the oldest sense: an aspirated consonant is a sound carrying a puff of breath.
normal.cn: 语音学保留了最古老的意思：送气辅音就是带出一口气的音。

abstract.en: Picture a child on a sill looking at a spire until the neck aches.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子趴在窗台上望着塔尖，直到脖子发酸。

abstract.en: Picture a kite pulling at the string before the wind has lifted it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只风筝在风还没把它托起时就已经把线拉紧。

abstract.en: Picture a seed leaning toward a light it cannot yet reach.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子朝它还够不到的光倾斜。

examples.en: Many young engineers aspire to work on the rover team.
examples.cn: 许多年轻工程师立志进入火星车团队。

examples.en: He aspired to the mayor's office for twelve years.
examples.cn: 他谋求市长之位谋了十二年。

examples.en: The village aspired after clean water more than after roads.
examples.cn: 村民对干净用水的渴求胜过对道路的渴求。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「a 斯派尔」——一口气朝远处送去 → 立志、渴望

root: 拉丁 aspirare「朝……呼气」= ad-（向）+ spirare（呼吸）；spirare 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one breath: it is aimed at a goal, at an office, at an identity, at a model, at a condition, at the sky itself, at a consonant, and finally at something simply out of reach.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一口气展开：这口气被呼向一个目标、一个职位、一种身份、一个榜样、一种处境、天空本身、一个辅音，最后呼向一件单纯够不到的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a watcher at a window breathing toward a distant spire.
core.cn: 核心意象：窗前的观望者朝远处塔尖呼出一口气。

branches.en: THE AIM AND THE CONDITION: a distant goal and a wished-for state are the same upward breath.
branches.cn: 目标与处境：远处的目标与所盼的处境，是同一口向上的气。

branches.en: THE CONTESTED SEAT: others want it too, and the political origin shows.
branches.cn: 被争的位子：别人也想要，政治来源在此显现。

branches.en: A SELF TO BUILD: a person and a model are both aims one grows toward.
branches.cn: 待建的自己：人与榜样都是会长过去的靶子。

branches.en: THE LITERAL RISE: stone and smoke go up before desire is meant.
branches.cn: 字面的升起：在「渴望」之前，石头与烟先往上升。

branches.en: BREATH WITHOUT AN OBJECT: a consonant's puff, and longing that has given up on arrival.
branches.cn: 没有对象的气：辅音的那一口气，以及不再指望抵达的渴望。

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb with a prepositional prefix, and both parts still build English words, so it reads clearly by morphemes.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个带介词前缀的拉丁动词，两部分仍在构成英语词，因此可以按语素清楚读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin spirare gives spirit, inspire, expire, respire and conspire; ad- 'to' appears in adapt, adhere and admire.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 spirare 衍生出 spirit、inspire、expire、respire 与 conspire；ad-「向」见于 adapt、adhere 与 admire。

items.example: The prefix gives the breath a direction.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀给这口气一个方向。

items.example: The root is the breathing itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根就是呼吸本身。

items.example: The wind breathed upon the cliff.

items.structure: aspirare passing into French and English
items.example: She aspired to the research post.
items.exampleCN: 她立志争取这个研究职位。

items.example: An aspiring novelist worked the night shift.
items.exampleCN: 一位有志写小说的人上夜班。
四名谋求者进入候选名单。

items.example: His aspiration was to teach in the hills.
items.exampleCN: 他的志向是在山里教书。

items.example: The brochure was aspirational, not literal.
items.exampleCN: 这本宣传册是在引发向往，而非写实。

items.example: Children aspirate the first consonant too strongly.
items.exampleCN: 孩子们把第一个辅音送气送得太重。

items.example: The valley inspired the whole score.
items.exampleCN: 这条山谷激发了整部乐曲。

definition_zh: n. 阿司匹林（乙酰水杨酸，止痛退热药）；一片阿司匹林
definition_en: A common medicine that relieves pain and fever and thins the blood; also a single tablet of that medicine.
core_image: 掌心一片白色小圆药片
scene: 他为了头痛服下一片白色药片。He took an aspirin for the headache.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：aspirin 指那种止痛退热的药本身，作为物质名词不可数。

pos.zh: 阿司匹林；阿司匹林药片

senses.title: The medicine itself
senses.definition: the substance that eases pain, lowers fever and reduces clotting, used as an uncountable noun
senses.definitionCN: 缓解疼痛、退烧并减少凝血的物质，作不可数名词使用
senses.example: Low doses of aspirin are sometimes prescribed for the heart.
senses.exampleCN: 医生有时开小剂量阿司匹林用于心脏。
senses.why: The name hides a plant: the middle part comes from a shrub whose bark first gave the acid.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字里藏着一株植物：中间部分来自一种灌木，其树皮最早提供了这种酸。

senses.title: One tablet of it
senses.definition: a single measured piece of the medicine, the countable use
senses.definitionCN: 这种药的一片定量制剂，是可数用法
senses.example: She swallowed two aspirins with water.
senses.exampleCN: 她就水吞下两片阿司匹林。
senses.why: English often turns a substance into a countable unit once it comes in fixed pieces, as with coffee and aspirin.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把物质名词在有了固定份量后变成可数单位，coffee 与 aspirin 都是如此。

intro.en: Aspirin was a trade name coined in 1899: a- for the acetyl group, spir- from the shrub Spiraea that yielded the acid, and -in as a common drug ending.
intro.cn: aspirin 是 1899 年造出的商品名：a- 代表乙酰基，spir- 取自提供该酸的绣线菊属植物，-in 则是常见的药名后缀。

items.en: Latin salix meant willow, whose bark had been chewed for pain and fever since ancient times.
items.cn: 拉丁语 salix 意为「柳树」，自古以来人们就嚼柳树皮来止痛退烧。

items.en: Greek speira meant a coil or twist, and gave the shrub name Spiraea for its twisted seed pods.
items.cn: 希腊语 speira 意为「盘绕」，因绣线菊的种荚扭曲而成为该属植物名。

items.en: Meadowsweet, a shrub of that group, also carried the pain-relieving acid in its flowers.
items.cn: 同属的蚊子草花中也含有这种止痛的酸。

items.en: Chemists isolated the acid in the 1830s and named it after the plant, but it burned the stomach.
items.cn: 化学家在十九世纪三十年代分离出这种酸并以植物命名，但它刺激胃部。

items.en: Adding an acetyl group in 1897 produced a gentler compound that kept the effect.
items.cn: 1897 年加上乙酰基后得到一种更温和却仍有效的化合物。

items.en: The name was registered in 1899 and later lost its protected status in several countries, becoming an ordinary word.
items.cn: 这个名字于 1899 年注册，后来在若干国家失去商标保护，变成普通词。

note.en: The look-alike group warns against the aspire family, which is unrelated, and shows the plant behind the name; the near-meaning group lists neighbouring drugs.
note.cn: 形近组提醒不要与毫无亲缘的 aspire 一族混淆，并展示名字背后的植物；近义组列出邻近的药物。

entries.definition: To aim at something high or difficult.
To fill someone with a feeling or idea.
entries.definitionCN: 把某种感受或想法注入某人心中。

entries.definition: A shrub whose flowers gave the acid.
A medicine that stops blood clotting.
A medicine that relieves pain.
A drug taken to stop pain.
Another common pain and fever medicine.
entries.definitionCN: 另一种常用止痛退热药。

entries.definition: A common medicine for fever and pain.

normalIntro.en: Aspirin is a- for acetyl, spir- from the shrub name, and -in for a drug: a plant acid wearing a chemical hat.
normalIntro.cn: aspirin 是 a-「乙酰」加 spir-「绣线菊」再加 -in「药名」：一株植物的酸戴上了化学的帽子。

normal.en: Aspirin has nothing to do with aspire.
normal.cn: aspirin 与 aspire 毫无关系。

normal.en: Uncountable for the drug, countable for tablets.
normal.cn: 指药物时不可数，指药片时可数。

normal.en: The ending -in marks many drug names.
normal.cn: 后缀 -in 出现在许多药名中。

normal.en: The acid first came from willow bark.
normal.cn: 这种酸最早来自柳树皮。

normal.en: It relieves pain, fever and clotting at once.
normal.cn: 它同时缓解疼痛、发热与凝血。

abstract.en: Picture a small white disc in an open palm.
abstract.cn: 想象摊开的掌心里一片白色小圆片。

abstract.en: Imagine bark stripped from a willow by a river.
abstract.cn: 想象河边柳树上被剥下的树皮。

abstract.en: Think of a twisted seed pod naming a medicine.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚扭曲的种荚给一种药命了名。

examples.en: The nurse handed him an aspirin.
examples.cn: 护士递给他一片阿司匹林。

examples.en: Aspirin can irritate an empty stomach.
examples.cn: 阿司匹林会刺激空腹的胃。

examples.en: He keeps aspirins in his coat pocket.
examples.cn: 他外套口袋里常备着阿司匹林药片。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：a「乙酰」+ spir「绣线菊」+ in「药」——从植物里提出来、戴上乙酰帽子的止痛药 aspirin。

root: 拉丁语 salix「柳树」与希腊语 speira「盘绕」分别指向柳树皮与绣线菊；1897 年加乙酰基得到温和的水杨酸衍生物，1899 年以 a- + spir- + -in 注册为药名 aspirin。

sensesIntro.en: The two senses are one white disc seen twice: as a substance measured in doses, and as a countable tablet in the hand.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一片白色小圆片被看了两遍：作为按剂量计的物质，以及手里可数的一片药。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small white disc resting in an open palm
core.cn: 核心意象：掌心一片白色小圆药片

branches.en: A low daily dose for the heart.
branches.cn: 为心脏开的小剂量每日服药。

branches.en: A white disc in a coat pocket.
branches.cn: 外套口袋里的一片白药片。

branches.en: One substance, counted only once tableted.
branches.cn: 同一种物质，压成片后才可数。

intro.en: Aspirin is a chemical coinage: a- for acetyl, spir- from a plant name, -in for a substance; the medical field around it is Greek.
intro.cn: aspirin 是化学造词：a-「乙酰」、spir-「植物名」、-in「物质」；它周围的医学词汇多为希腊来源。

latinIntro.en: The classical layer is Latin salix, willow, and acidum, sour; Greek speira, a coil, named the shrub that gave the acid.
latinIntro.cn: 古典层次是拉丁语 salix「柳树」与 acidum「酸的」；希腊语 speira「盘绕」则为提供该酸的灌木命名。

latinEntries.example: Salix names the bark first used.
latinEntries.exampleCN: salix 指最早使用的树皮来源。
acidum 产生 acid 与 acidic。
spira 为扭曲的种荚命名。

definition_zh: v. 猛烈攻击；抨击；（疑虑、气味等）强烈困扰
definition_en: To attack someone violently, with blows or with words; of doubts, fears or smells, to trouble someone strongly and suddenly.
core_image: 一群人朝一个方向扑上去，问题像拳头一样砸过来
scene: 记者们一拥而上，连番追问。Reporters assailed the minister with questions.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：assail 指用言辞或拳脚猛烈攻击，常用 assail someone with something。

senses.title: To attack with blows or words
senses.definition: to set upon someone violently, whether physically or in fierce argument
senses.definitionCN: 猛烈扑向某人，可以是动手，也可以是激烈的言辞交锋
senses.example: Critics assailed the plan from every side.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者从各个角度猛攻这个方案。
senses.why: The root means to leap, so the word keeps the picture of a body jumping at its target rather than merely striking it.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为「跳」，所以这个词保留的是身体朝目标扑上去的画面，而不只是打击。

senses.title: To trouble strongly
senses.definition: of doubts, fears, smells or noise, to come at someone suddenly and hard to resist
senses.definitionCN: 指疑虑、恐惧、气味或噪音突然袭来，令人难以抵挡
senses.example: Doubts assailed her as she signed the form.
senses.exampleCN: 签表格时疑虑一阵阵袭上她心头。
senses.why: Here the attacker is not a person: the feeling itself leaps at you, which is why the passive is so common.
senses.whyCN: 这里攻击者不是人：情绪本身朝你扑来，这也是被动式如此常见的原因。

intro.en: Assail is Latin assilire, from ad, at, plus salire, to leap: to leap at someone, through Old French asalir.
intro.cn: assail 就是拉丁语 assilire，由 ad「向」加 salire「跳」构成：朝某人扑上去，经古法语 asalir 传入英语。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning to jump lies behind several words for leaping and for sudden attack.
items.cn: 一个拟构词根意为「跳」，藏在若干表示跳跃与突袭的词背后。

items.en: Latin salire meant to leap or spring, and gives salient, something that leaps out at you.
items.cn: 拉丁语 salire 意为「跳、跃」，产生 salient「跳到你眼前的」，即「显著的」。

items.en: With ad, at, assilire meant to leap at, to spring upon an enemy.
items.cn: 加上 ad「向」之后，assilire 意为「扑向」，即朝敌人跃去。

items.en: Old French asalir kept the sense of violent attack and lost the visible leap.
items.cn: 古法语 asalir 保留了猛攻的意思，却丢掉了「跳」的可见形象。

items.en: Middle English assailen meant to attack in battle, and the modern spelling settled later.
items.cn: 中古英语 assailen 意为在战斗中攻击，现代拼写后来才定型。

items.en: By the sixteenth century doubts and fears could assail a person, moving the verb inside the mind.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，疑虑与恐惧也能 assail 一个人，把这个动词搬进了内心。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the leaping root and its relatives; the near-meaning group grades attacks by how they arrive.
note.cn: 形近组保留「跳」词根及其亲属；近义组按「攻击如何到来」区分。

entries.definition: A sudden violent attack.
The person who attacks someone.
Most noticeable, as if leaping out.
entries.definitionCN: 最显眼的，仿佛跳到眼前。

entries.definition: To rejoice openly and energetically.
To act violently against someone.
To trouble from every side at once.
To attack continuously without pause.
To take a place by sudden force.
entries.definitionCN: 以突发的武力夺取某地。

normalIntro.en: Assail is ad, at, plus salire, leap: leaping at someone, with fists, with words or with doubts.
normalIntro.cn: assail 就是 ad「向」加 salire「跳」：朝人扑上去，用拳头、用言辞，或用疑虑。

normal.en: Assail someone with something is the pattern.
normal.cn: 句式是 assail someone with something。

normal.en: Assailant names the attacker.
normal.cn: assailant 指攻击者。

normal.en: Assault is the noun from the same root.
normal.cn: assault 是同根的名词。

normal.en: Doubts assail you, so the passive is common.
normal.cn: 疑虑会袭来，所以被动式常见。

normal.en: Unassailable means nothing can leap at it.
normal.cn: unassailable 意为无从下手攻击。

abstract.en: Picture microphones thrust at one face.
abstract.cn: 想象话筒一齐戳向一张脸。

abstract.en: Imagine doubts jumping at you mid-signature.
abstract.cn: 想象签字签到一半疑虑扑上来。

abstract.en: Think of a smell that hits before you see it.
abstract.cn: 想象还没看见就先撞上来的气味。

examples.en: The crowd assailed the gates at dusk.
examples.cn: 黄昏时人群猛攻大门。

examples.en: She was assailed by a smell of burning.
examples.cn: 一股焦味猛然袭向她。

examples.en: Opponents assailed every clause of the bill.
examples.cn: 反对者猛攻议案的每一条款。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：as-「向」+ sail「跳」（同 salire）——朝人扑上去就是 assail；名词形式便是 assault。

root: 拉丁语 salire「跳」加 ad-「向」构成 assilire「扑向」，经古法语 asalir 入中古英语 assailen；同根还有 assault「袭击」、assailant「攻击者」与 salient「显著的」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one leap at a target: a crowd jumping at a person, and a feeling jumping at the mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都是朝目标的一次扑击：人群扑向一个人，情绪扑向内心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crowd leaping at one point, questions landing like blows
core.cn: 核心意象：一群人朝一处扑上去，问题像拳头一样砸过来

branches.cn: 一齐戳向一张脸的话筒。

branches.en: A crowd pressing at the gates.
A smell of burning hitting first.
Both come at you faster than you can answer.
branches.cn: 两者都来得比你回应更快。

intro.en: Assail is as- from ad- plus -sail from salire, leap; the same root builds assault, salient, exult and result.
intro.cn: assail 由 ad- 变来的 as- 加出自 salire「跳」的 -sail 构成；同一词根还构成 assault、salient、exult 与 result。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is salire, to leap, assilire, to leap at, and saltus, a leap; the agent ending -ant gives assailant.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 salire「跳」、assilire「扑向」与 saltus「一跃」；施事后缀 -ant 给出 assailant。

definition_zh: 刺客；暗杀者
definition_en: a person who kills an important person suddenly and secretly for payment or a cause

sceneCN: 这里 assassin 是「刺客」（第 1 个义项：受人指使秘密行凶者）；句意是刺客在桥上等候公爵的马车。

senses.title: A secret political killer
senses.definition: one who murders a prominent figure by surprise attack
senses.definitionCN: 以突然袭击谋杀显要人物的人
senses.example: History books record the assassin who shot the archduke in Sarajevo.
senses.exampleCN: 史书记载了在萨拉热窝枪击大公的刺客。

senses.title: Any hired or secret killer
senses.definition: any person paid or persuaded to kill secretly
senses.definitionCN: 受雇或受唆使秘密杀人者
senses.example: The novel's assassin never misses his mark.
senses.exampleCN: 小说里的杀手弹无虚发。
senses.why: From the political case the word widened to every stealthy contract killer.
