intro.en: Assassin comes through French and Italian from Arabic hashshashin, users of hashish, a name given to a medieval sect of political killers.
intro.cn: assassin 经法语、意大利语源自阿拉伯语 hashshāshīn（吸食大麻者），是外界对一个中世纪暗杀派别的称呼。

items.en: Hashshashin meant users of hashish, applied to the Nizari Ismaili order in Persia and Syria.
items.cn: hashshāshīn 意为「服食哈希什者」，用于波斯和叙利亚的尼扎里派。

items.en: Crusader writers popularized stories of drugged killers obeying a hidden master.
items.cn: 十字军编年史作者传播了「服药杀手听命于隐秘主人」的故事。

items.en: Italian assassino carried the word through trade and travel writing.
items.cn: 意大利语 assassino 经商旅与游记传播该词。

items.en: French assassin entered literary use.
items.cn: 法语 assassin 进入文学用语。

items.en: English adopted assassin in the sixteenth century; the verb followed shortly after.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语借入 assassin，动词形式随后出现。

note.en: The word's drug story is colorful but partly legend; what is sure is the Arabic tribal-political source.
note.cn: 「服毒行凶」的故事色彩浓烈但半属传说；可以肯定的是其阿拉伯语的政治派别来源。

normalIntro.cn: 「额赛星」→联想「暗舍心」：藏身暗舍、心存杀机，即是 assassin（刺客）。

intro.en: Assassin stands as a lone borrowing; its family grows by English suffixes, not Latin roots.
intro.cn: assassin 是孤立的外来词；其词族靠英语后缀扩展，而非拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: No Latin cognates: the source is Arabic.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁同源词：来源是阿拉伯语。

definition_zh: n. 暗杀；行刺（尤指政治人物）；（名誉的）毁谤
definition_en: The murder of a prominent person, usually for political reasons; figuratively, the deliberate destruction of a reputation.
core_image: 一声枪响之后，一个位置突然空了
scene: 广播里传来总统遇刺的消息。The radio reported the assassination of the president.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：assassination 指出于政治等目的杀害重要人物。

senses.title: The killing of a prominent person
senses.definition: the deliberate murder of a public figure, usually to change or punish a political order
senses.definitionCN: 有意杀害公众人物，通常为了改变或惩罚某种政治秩序
senses.example: The assassination plunged the country into mourning.
senses.exampleCN: 这次暗杀使全国陷入哀悼。
senses.why: What separates this word from murder is the target: the victim matters to many people, so the act is public.
senses.whyCN: 把这个词与 murder 区分开的是目标：受害者对许多人都有分量，所以这一行为是公共性的。

senses.title: The killing of a reputation
senses.definition: a sustained attempt to destroy someone standing, as in the phrase character assassination
senses.definitionCN: 持续地摧毁某人的声望，如「人格毁谤」这一说法
senses.example: The campaign was character assassination, not debate.
senses.exampleCN: 那场攻势是人格毁谤，不是辩论。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the essentials: a chosen target, a planned strike and something that cannot be brought back.
senses.whyCN: 这个隐喻保留了核心要素：选定的目标、有计划的打击，以及无法挽回的东西。

intro.en: Assassination comes from assassin, traced by the traditional account to Arabic hashshashin, a name applied to a secretive order in Persia and Syria.
intro.cn: assassination 出自 assassin；按传统说法，后者源自阿拉伯语 hashshashin，是对波斯与叙利亚一个秘密教团的称呼。

items.en: The traditional account links the word to a name for a secretive order whose members carried out targeted killings.
items.cn: 传统说法把这个词与一个秘密教团的称号相联，其成员执行有目标的杀害。

items.en: Crusaders brought back stories and the name, and the tale of drug use is now doubted by historians.
items.cn: 十字军带回故事与这个称号，而其中「用药」的说法如今已被史家质疑。

items.en: Medieval Latin assassinus named a hired killer, stripping the word of its sect and keeping the act.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 assassinus 指受雇的杀手，剥去教团背景，只留下行为本身。

items.en: Italian assassinare turned the noun into a verb meaning to murder a prominent person.
items.cn: 意大利语 assassinare 把名词变成动词，意为杀害重要人物。

items.en: English records the noun from the mid seventeenth century, soon standard in political reporting.
items.cn: 英语从十七世纪中叶起记录这个名词，很快成为政治报道的标准用词。

items.en: Nineteenth-century journalism fixed character assassination for the planned ruin of a name.
items.cn: 十九世纪新闻业固定了 character assassination 一语，指有计划地毁掉一个人的名声。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the assassin family and adds a word that only sounds similar; the near-meaning group grades killings by scale and framing.
note.cn: 形近组保留 assassin 词族，并加上一个只是听着像的词；近义组按规模与说法区分各种杀害。

normalIntro.en: Assassination is assassin plus -ation: the act named after the doer, and the doer named after an old order.
normalIntro.cn: assassination 就是 assassin 加 -ation：以行为者命名的行为，而行为者又以一个古老教团命名。

normal.en: Assassin, assassinate, assassination form one chain.
normal.cn: assassin、assassinate、assassination 是一条链。

normal.en: The target must be a public figure.
normal.cn: 目标必须是公众人物。

normal.en: An assassination attempt is a failed one.
normal.cn: an assassination attempt 指未成功的行刺。

normal.en: Character assassination attacks a name, not a body.
normal.cn: character assassination 攻击名声，不是身体。

normal.en: Murder is the wider word, this one is specific.
normal.cn: murder 更宽泛，本词更具体。

abstract.en: Picture one shot and one empty chair.
abstract.cn: 想象一声枪响与一把空椅子。

abstract.en: Imagine a whole street lowering its flags.
abstract.cn: 想象整条街降下半旗。

abstract.en: Think of a name torn down line by line.
abstract.cn: 想象一个名字被一行行撕掉。

examples.en: He called the article character assassination.

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：assassin「刺客」+ -ation「行为」——刺客干的那件事，就是暗杀 assassination。

root: 阿拉伯语 hashshashin 经十字军传闻与中世纪拉丁语 assassinus 变成「受雇杀手」，意大利语 assassinare 转为动词，英语加 -ation 于十七世纪中叶构成 assassination。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses destroy something public and irreplaceable: a person who held a position, and a name that took years to build.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都摧毁某种公共而不可替代之物：占据某个位置的人，以及多年才建立起来的名声。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one shot, and a public place suddenly empty
core.cn: 核心意象：一声枪响之后，一个位置突然空了

intro.en: Assassination is assassin plus -ation through the verb -ate; the surrounding political vocabulary is built from -al, -ist and -ism.
intro.cn: assassination 是 assassin 经动词后缀 -ate 再加 -ation 构成；周边的政治词汇由 -al、-ist 与 -ism 搭起。

latinIntro.en: The word is Arabic at heart, but Medieval Latin assassinus and assassinare carried it into Europe; Latin caedes, slaughter, names the act beside it.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词内核来自阿拉伯语，但中世纪拉丁语 assassinus 与 assassinare 把它带进欧洲；旁边的拉丁语 caedes「杀戮」指同一行为。

definition_zh: n. 猛攻；袭击；侵犯人身罪；v. 袭击；猛烈抨击
definition_en: A sudden violent attack, or the crime of attacking or threatening someone; as a verb, to attack physically or to criticise fiercely.
core_image: 一只手突然挥过来，或者一道防线被硬生生撞开
scene: 他因在酒吧外动手伤人被起诉。He was charged with assault outside the bar.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：assault 在法律上指侵犯人身的罪名，不一定要造成重伤。

senses.title: A sudden violent attack
senses.definition: a forceful attack on a person or a place, the older military and physical sense
senses.definitionCN: 对人或地点的强力攻击，是较早的军事与身体义
senses.example: The assault on the walls began at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 对城墙的猛攻在黎明开始。
senses.why: The root means to leap, so an assault is a jump at a wall or a body rather than a slow siege.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为「跳」，所以 assault 是朝城墙或身体的一跃，而不是缓慢的围困。

senses.title: The crime against a person
senses.definition: in law, an act that attacks or threatens another person, which need not cause serious injury
senses.definitionCN: 法律上指攻击或威胁他人的行为，不必造成重伤
senses.example: He pleaded guilty to common assault.
senses.exampleCN: 他承认普通侵犯人身罪。
senses.why: The legal sense narrowed the word to a defined offence, which is why it appears in charges and reports.
senses.whyCN: 法律义把这个词收窄为一项确定的罪名，所以它出现在起诉与判决书中。

senses.title: To attack or criticise fiercely
senses.definition: as a verb, to attack someone physically, or to attack a policy or idea in strong terms
senses.definitionCN: 作动词指动手袭击某人，或用强烈言辞攻击某项政策或观点
senses.example: The report assaults the whole funding model.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告猛攻整套资助模式。
senses.why: The verb keeps both fronts open, so a policy can be assaulted exactly as a gate can.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词两条战线都留着，所以一项政策可以像一道城门那样被 assault。

intro.en: Assault is Latin assultus, from assilire, to leap at, formed from ad, at, plus salire, to leap; Old French asaut lost the l that scholars later restored.
intro.cn: assault 就是拉丁语 assultus，出自 assilire「扑向」，由 ad「向」加 salire「跳」构成；古法语 asaut 丢掉的 l 后来被学者补回。

items.en: Latin salire meant to leap, the physical core shared with assail and salient.
items.cn: 拉丁语 salire 意为「跳」，是与 assail、salient 共有的身体内核。

items.en: With ad, at, assilire meant to spring upon, and its noun assultus named the springing.
items.cn: 加上 ad「向」后，assilire 意为「跃上」，其名词 assultus 指那一跃。

items.en: Old French asaut meant a violent attack and dropped the l of the Latin form.
items.cn: 古法语 asaut 意为猛攻，并丢掉了拉丁形式中的 l。

items.en: Middle English assaut named both a military storming and a personal attack.
items.cn: 中古英语 assaut 既指军事强攻，也指对人身的攻击。

items.en: Sixteenth-century writers put the l back to match Latin, giving the modern spelling.
items.cn: 十六世纪的书写者为对齐拉丁语把 l 补回，形成现代拼写。

items.en: English law then fixed assault as a named offence, distinct from the actual striking called battery.
items.cn: 此后英国法把 assault 定为一项罪名，与实际动手的 battery 相区别。

note.en: The look-alike group warns that result, insult and consult only share sounds; the near-meaning group separates the attack, the ambush and the legal pair.
note.cn: 形近组提醒 result、insult、consult 只是音近；近义组把猛攻、伏击与法律上的一对罪名分开。

normalIntro.en: Assault is the noun cousin of assail: the same leap at a target, frozen into a thing you can name in court.
normalIntro.cn: assault 是 assail 的名词表亲：同样朝目标一跃，只是被定格成能在法庭上指称的一件事。

normal.en: An assault on something is the usual pattern.
normal.cn: 常见句式是 an assault on something。

normal.en: In law, assault and battery are different charges.
normal.cn: 法律上 assault 与 battery 是不同罪名。

normal.en: The verb takes a direct object: assault a guard.
normal.cn: 动词直接带宾语：assault a guard。

normal.en: Assail is the verb form with the same root.
normal.cn: assail 是同根的动词形式。

normal.en: The l was put back to look like Latin.
normal.cn: 那个 l 是为了像拉丁语才补回的。

abstract.en: Picture a hand swinging before you can step back.
abstract.cn: 想象你还来不及后退就挥过来的一只手。

abstract.en: Imagine ladders hitting a wall at first light.
abstract.cn: 想象天刚亮就搭上城墙的梯子。

abstract.en: Think of a report landing like a blow.
abstract.cn: 想象一份报告像拳头一样落下。

examples.en: The assault left the door hanging open.
examples.cn: 猛攻之后门被撞得敞着。

examples.en: She reported the assault to the police.
examples.cn: 她向警方报了这起袭击。

examples.en: Columnists assaulted the new tax.
examples.cn: 专栏作者猛攻新税。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：as-「向」+ sault「跳」——朝人跃过去的那一下，就是袭击 assault；同根动词是 assail。

root: 拉丁语 salire「跳」加 ad-「向」构成 assilire「扑向」，名词 assultus 经古法语 asaut 入英语，十六世纪补回 l 成 assault；十七世纪法律把它定为罪名。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses are one leap at a target: storming a wall, the offence named in a charge, and the verb that does it to bodies or to policies.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项都是朝目标的一次扑击：强攻城墙、起诉状里的罪名，以及作用于身体或政策的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand swinging out, or a line forced open
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手突然挥过来，或一道防线被硬生生撞开

branches.en: Ladders hitting a wall at dawn.
A door forced open by the rush.
A charge read out in court.
A report landing like a blow.
branches.cn: 像拳头一样落下的报告。

branches.en: One leap, named as act, offence and verb.
branches.cn: 同一次扑击，被称作行为、罪名与动词。

intro.en: Assault is as- from ad- plus -sault from salire, leap; the same root builds assail, salient, insult and result.
intro.cn: assault 由 ad- 变来的 as- 加出自 salire「跳」的 -sault 构成；同一词根还构成 assail、salient、insult 与 result。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is salire, to leap, assilire, to leap at, and assultus, the leap itself; the agent ending -ant gives assailant.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 salire「跳」、assilire「扑向」与 assultus「那一跃」；施事后缀 -ant 给出 assailant。

latinEntries.meaning: to leap at, to spring upon
latinEntries.exampleCN: assilire 产生 assault 与 assail。

definition_zh: 集合；聚集；组装；装配
definition_en: to bring people together, or to fit parts together into a whole
core_image: 散落的零件一件件拼合成整体
scene: 操场上哨声一响，各班开始排队。The students assembled in the hall before noon.
sceneCN: 这里 assemble 是「集合」（第 1 个义项：人们聚到一处）；句意是学生们中午前在礼堂集合。

senses.title: To come together in a group
senses.definition: to gather people or to gather oneself in one place
senses.definitionCN: 把人聚到一处，或自身聚到一处
senses.example: The students assembled in the hall before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们中午前在礼堂集合。
senses.why: Old French assembler came from Latin ad simul, 'to the same place', so the word begins as a gathering.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 assembler 来自拉丁语 ad simul「到同一处」，所以这个词本义就是聚集。

senses.title: To fit parts into a whole
senses.definition: to put separate pieces together so they work as one
senses.definitionCN: 把分开的部件拼在一起，使其作为一个整体运作
senses.example: Workers assemble the engines by hand.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们手工组装发动机。
senses.why: If parts are gathered in the right order, the gathering becomes construction; the same verb serves both.
senses.whyCN: 若把零件按正确次序聚到一起，聚集就成了装配；同一个动词兼指两者。

intro.en: Assemble goes back to a Latin phrase meaning 'to the same place'.
intro.cn: assemble 可追溯到意为「到同一处」的拉丁短语。

items.en: simul meant 'together, at the same time'.
items.cn: simul 意为「一起、同时」。

items.en: ad simul meant 'to the same place'.

definition_zh: 断言；坚称；维护；主张（权利等）
definition_en: to state firmly that something is true, or to act so as to make one's rights or presence felt
core_image: 拍着桌子一字一顿说话的人
scene: 听证会上，他敲着桌面逐条为自己的清白申辩，寸步不让。The witness asserted her innocence before the committee.
sceneCN: 这里 assert 是「断言、坚称」（第 1 个义项：坚定地陈述）；句意是证人在委员会面前坚称自己无辜。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「断言；主张」
由动词加后缀构成，义为「自信而坚定的」

senses.title: To state firmly as true
senses.definition: to declare something positively and confidently, often without proof
senses.definitionCN: 肯定而自信地宣称，常不附带证明
senses.example: The article asserts that housing prices will fall next year.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章断言房价明年将下跌。
senses.why: Latin serere means to join or link; asserting is binding a claim to a statement as if attaching it by hand.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 serere 意为连接；assert 即用手把主张「系」在陈述上。

senses.title: To claim or defend rights
senses.definition: to make one's rights, power, or position felt and recognized
senses.definitionCN: 使自己的权利、权力或地位得到承认
senses.example: The union asserted its right to strike.
senses.exampleCN: 工会维护了罢工的权利。
senses.why: The same binding hand attaches one's standing to the world: you fasten your claim publicly.
senses.whyCN: 同一只系结之手把自身地位固定于世界：公开拴紧自己的主张。

senses.title: To make oneself noticed
senses.definition: to behave confidently so that others take notice, as in assert oneself
senses.definitionCN: 自信行事使他人注意到自己，如 assert oneself
senses.example: Quiet students must learn to assert themselves in seminars.
senses.exampleCN: 安静的学生必须学会在研讨课上大胆发言。
senses.why: Presence, like a claim, must be attached to the scene before it exists socially.
senses.whyCN: 存在感如主张，须先「系」于场景，方能在社交中成立。

intro.en: Assert comes from Latin asserere, to claim or affirm, from ad- plus serere, to join or bind.
intro.cn: assert 源自拉丁语 asserere（主张、申明），由 ad- 加 serere（连接、系结）构成。

items.en: The root *ser- meant to line up or bind together.
items.cn: 词根 *ser- 意为排成一行、系在一起。

items.en: Serere meant to join, enlace, or set in a row.
items.cn: 拉丁语 serere 意为连接、缠绕、排列。

items.en: Asserere meant to attach a claim, hence to affirm; in law, to claim a slave as free.
items.cn: asserere 意为附上主张，进而申明；法律上指主张奴隶为自由人。

items.en: Assertio named the affirmation itself.
items.cn: assertio 指申明行为本身。

items.en: English adopted assert in the seventeenth century for firm declaration.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语借入 assert，指坚定的宣告。

note.en: Assert states with force; it does not argue step by step like prove.
note.cn: assert 是有力的宣示，不像 prove 那样一步步论证。

entries.definition: a firm statement or claim
confident and direct in manner
to make one's presence felt
what is deserved, from the same serere family sense of attachment
entries.definitionCN: 应得的赏罚（同根族内的近形词）

normalIntro.en: Hear a-sort: asserting sorts the world and stakes your claim in place.
normalIntro.cn: 谐音「额瑟特」→「额竖帖」：额把主张竖成告帖钉在墙上，即 assert（断言）。

normal.en: serere ties; assert ties a claim down.
normal.cn: serere 是系结；assert 把主张系牢。

normal.en: assert oneself: make others notice you.
normal.cn: assert oneself：让他人注意到你。

normal.en: assertion is the noun of the claim.

abstract.en: Picture a claim nailed to a courtroom door.
abstract.cn: 想象一条主张被钉在法庭门上。

abstract.en: Feel your shoulders square as you speak.
abstract.cn: 体会发言时挺直的双肩。

abstract.en: See a row of linked rings: each statement joined in place.
abstract.cn: 看见一排相连的环：每个陈述各就其位。

examples.en: The coach asserted that the team would bounce back.
examples.cn: 教练断言球队会东山再起。

examples.en: Nations asserted sovereignty over the new waters.
examples.cn: 各国宣示了对新水域的主权。

examples.en: She had to assert herself in a room full of executives.
examples.cn: 她必须在一屋高管面前大胆表态。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额瑟特」——额把主张竖成告帖、钉牢于墙，正是 assert 的断言。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（朝向）+ serere（连接、系结）→ asserere「把主张系附上来，申明」，经后期拉丁语与法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Binding a claim to words becomes binding rights and presence to the world.

intro.en: The serere family lines up English words about joining and binding.

latinIntro.en: Latin serere generated a family of joining words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 serere 产出一族表示连接的词。

definition_zh: adj. 自信而坚定表达自我的；（作风）强硬张扬的
definition_en: Confidently stating your needs and opinions without being aggressive; of a manner or style, forceful and insistent.
core_image: 声音不高，但把自己的要求说得清清楚楚
scene: 她学会平静而坚定地说出自己的要求。She learned to be assertive without raising her voice.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：assertive 指敢于清楚表达自己，同时不侵犯别人。

pos.zh: 自信坚定的；强硬主张的

forms.label: 形容词原级（比较级用 more）

senses.title: Confident without aggression
senses.definition: able to state your needs and opinions clearly while still respecting other people
senses.definitionCN: 能清楚说出自己的需要与看法，同时仍尊重别人
senses.example: Being assertive is not the same as being rude.
senses.exampleCN: 敢于表达并不等于无礼。
senses.why: The root means to join a claim to yourself, so the word describes holding your own position, not pushing others off theirs.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为「把主张接到自己身上」，所以这个词说的是守住自己的位置，而不是把别人挤下去。

senses.title: Forceful in manner or style
senses.definition: of a tone, design or performance, insistent and unwilling to be overlooked
senses.definitionCN: 指语气、设计或表现气势逼人，不肯被忽视
senses.example: The wine has an assertive smoky flavour.
senses.exampleCN: 这款酒有一股张扬的烟熏味。
senses.why: Applied to things rather than people, the word loses its praise and simply means demanding attention.
senses.whyCN: 用于事物而非人时，这个词失去褒义，只表示「要求被注意」。

intro.en: Assertive comes from Latin asserere, from ad, to, plus serere, to join: to lay a hand on someone and claim their freedom, hence to claim firmly.
intro.cn: assertive 出自拉丁语 asserere，由 ad「向」加 serere「连接」构成：把手按在某人身上宣布其自由，因而引申为「坚定主张」。

items.en: Latin serere meant to join or bind in a row, and gives series and insert.
items.cn: 拉丁语 serere 意为「连接成排」，产生 series 与 insert。

items.en: With ad, to, asserere meant to join a claim to yourself, used in the formal freeing of a slave.
items.cn: 加上 ad「向」后，asserere 意为「把主张接到自己身上」，用于正式宣布奴隶获释的仪式。

items.en: The noun assertio named a formal claim of freedom, and later any firm statement.
items.cn: 名词 assertio 指正式的自由宣告，后来指任何坚定的陈述。

items.en: English took assert in the sixteenth century with the sense of stating firmly.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 assert，意为坚定地陈述。

items.en: The adjective assertive appears in the nineteenth century, at first often meaning merely dogmatic.
items.cn: 形容词 assertive 出现于十九世纪，起初常只表示「独断」。

items.en: Psychology in the 1970s made assertiveness a skill between passivity and aggression, giving the word its praise.
items.cn: 二十世纪七十年代的心理学把「敢于表达」定为介于被动与攻击之间的技能，赋予这个词褒义。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses hold a position firmly: a person stating a claim without aggression, and a taste or design that refuses to be overlooked.

definition_zh: 评估；估算；核定（税额）
definition_en: to judge the value or quality of something, or to set a tax on it
core_image: 法官身旁有人翻着卷宗，为每件事标出分量
scene: 保险公司派人来看被水泡过的墙。An engineer came to assess the damage.
sceneCN: 这里 assess 是「评估」（第 1 个义项：判断情况的性质与程度）；句意是工程师来评估损失程度。

pos.zh: 动词：评估；估算；核定（税额）

senses.title: Judge value or quality
senses.definition: to judge or decide the amount, value or quality of something
senses.definitionCN: 判断某事的数量、价值或好坏
senses.example: An engineer came to assess the damage.
senses.exampleCN: 一位工程师来评估损失。
senses.why: Assess comes from Latin assidere 'to sit beside', originally of an assistant sitting next to a judge, so the core act is sitting down to weigh a case.
senses.whyCN: assess 源自拉丁语 assidere「坐在旁边」，原指坐在法官身旁协助断案，核心动作就是坐下来衡量一桩事情。

senses.title: Set a tax or fine
senses.definition: to calculate and set the amount of a tax or fine to be paid
senses.definitionCN: 计算并确定应缴的税额或罚款
senses.example: The city assesses a tax on every rented flat.
senses.exampleCN: 市里对每套出租房征税。
senses.why: The act of weighing value entered the treasury: once a property's worth is judged, a tax can be fixed on it, and that fixing became a sense of its own.
senses.whyCN: 衡量价值的动作进入财政领域：先判定财产值多少，再据此定税，这个「定额」的环节单独成了一个义项。

intro.en: Assess began as a word about sitting beside a judge and ended as a word about weighing value.
intro.cn: assess 起初指坐在法官身旁，最后变成衡量价值的词。

items.en: assidere meant 'to sit beside', used of a judge's assistant.
items.cn: assidere 意为「坐在旁边」，用于说法官的助手。

items.en: assessus was the one who sat beside and helped fix a penalty.
items.cn: assessus 指坐在旁边协助定罚的人。

items.en: assessare meant 'to fix the amount of a tax'.
items.cn: assessare 意为「核定税额」。

items.en: English assessen kept the tax sense, valuing property for payment.
items.cn: 英语 assessen 保留税务义，为征税而估定财产价值。

items.en: The sense widened from tax to any judgement of value or quality.
items.cn: 词义从税务扩大到对任何事物的价值与质量作出判断。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the assess shape; the near-meaning group gives other verbs of judging value.
note.cn: 形近组与 assess 外形相近；近义组是其他表示估值的动词。

abstract.cn: 想象一只手把卷宗放上铜天平称量。

abstract.en: See a stamp pressed onto a property list, fixing a figure.
abstract.cn: 想象印章压在房产清单上，定下一个数目。

abstract.en: See a doctor reading a chart before speaking.
abstract.cn: 想象医生先看完病历再开口。

examples.en: An engineer came to assess the damage.
examples.cn: 一位工程师来评估损失。

examples.en: The city assesses a tax on every rented flat.
examples.cn: 市里对每套出租房征税。

examples.en: Teachers assess students on both writing and speaking.
examples.cn: 老师从写作和口语两方面评估学生。

dict_mnemonic.text: as-（在旁）加 sess（坐）：坐在旁边替人衡量，就是评估；衡量财产以定税，就是核定税额。

root: 源自拉丁语 assidere「坐在旁边」，经中世纪拉丁语 assessare「核定税额」进入英语，由「坐在法官身旁断案」引申为评估，再专指核定税额。

sensesIntro.en: Weighing a situation and fixing a tax are two stages of the same seated judgement.
sensesIntro.cn: 衡量情况与核定税额，是同一个「坐下来判断」的两个阶段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure written beside a case after it has been weighed.

intro.en: Assess is built on the Latin verb for sitting, and the same root runs through session and preside.
intro.cn: assess 建立在拉丁语「坐」的动词上，同一词根贯穿 session 与 preside。

latinIntro.en: The root sess or sid, 'to sit', comes from Latin sedere.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 sess 或 sid 意为「坐」，来自拉丁语 sedere。
